items.title: Tchad : Saleh Kebzabo dément des propos alarmistes sur une prétendue guerre civile

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : Saleh Kebzabo dément des propos alarmistes sur une prétendue guerre civile
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
Tchad : Saleh Kebzabo dément des propos alarmistes sur une prétendue guerre civile
La Médiature de la République au Tchad a démenti tout propos alarmiste attribué à l'ambassadeur Saleh Kebzabo concernant un risque de guerre civile, appelant les médias à la rigueur.
Alwihda Info
27 nov. 2026
© DR
La Médiature de la République a vivement démenti, vendredi 27 novembre, les propos alarmistes attribués à son responsable, l'ambassadeur Saleh Kebzabo, par un média en ligne.
Dans un communiqué officiel, l'institution rejette l'attribution d'une mise en garde contre le risque d'une « guerre civile armée généralisée » au Tchad. Elle déplore des « raccourcis » dénaturant le sens de l'intervention de son représentant.
La mise au point fait suite à une rencontre organisée le mercredi 25 novembre à N'Djamena. Saleh Kebzabo y avait réuni des acteurs de la société civile, des journalistes, des universitaires et des représentants de think tanks pour présenter la stratégie d'engagement de la Médiature en faveur de la paix.
Selon le communiqué, les échanges ont notamment porté sur la circulation des armes et les conflits intercommunautaires. L'institution rappelle que l'ambassadeur a répondu avec responsabilité, plaidant pour l'implication de toutes les forces vives dans la cohésion sociale.
Tout en appelant les médias et les acteurs des réseaux sociaux à la rigueur, la Médiature rappelle que « la paix est une responsabilité collective » qui ne peut s'accommoder de propos déformés.

items.title: Tchad : l'aide humanitaire atteint 2,5 millions de personnes malgré un déficit de financement

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : l'aide humanitaire atteint 2,5 millions de personnes malgré un déficit de financement
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
Tchad : l'aide humanitaire atteint 2,5 millions de personnes malgré un déficit de financement
Au Tchad, 2,5 millions de personnes ont reçu une assistance humanitaire au troisième trimestre 2026. Malgré des progrès, le plan de réponse reste confronté à d'importants manques de financements.
Alwihda Info
27 nov. 2026
© DR
En 2026, environ 4,5 millions de personnes ont besoin d’une assistance humanitaire au Tchad, dont 3,4 millions ont été ciblées dans le cadre du Plan de réponse humanitaire (HNRP), rapporte le  Bureau des affaires humanitaires de l'ONU . Face aux restrictions budgétaires, les acteurs humanitaires ont dû reprioriser leurs interventions pour se concentrer sur 1,9 million de personnes aux besoins les plus critiques.
Au 30 septembre 2026, environ 2,5 millions de personnes ont pu bénéficier d’une aide dans au moins un secteur, soit 75 % de la cible initiale. Parmi elles, 1,4 million présentent des besoins prioritaires, ce qui représente 74 % des personnes repriorisées.
Un financement partiel
Avec 456,3 millions de dollars mobilisés, les partenaires disposent de 46,3 % des besoins financiers globaux évalués pour le HNRP. Ces fonds ont permis de cibler en priorité les interventions vitales. Malgré ces efforts, près d’un million de personnes dans le besoin restent privées d’assistance.
La mobilisation de ressources supplémentaires demeure indispensable pour atteindre un demi-million de personnes vivant dans des zones sous haute tension humanitaire. Le rapport souligne par ailleurs de fortes disparités de financement selon les secteurs : la coordination et la gestion des camps (6,9 %), la réponse aux réfugiés (10,1 %) et la nutrition (29,3 %) affichent les taux de couverture les plus bas, illustrant la vulnérabilité persistante de la réponse au troisième trimestre 2026.

items.title: ORGEP : Idriss Dokony Adiker dément des transferts vers son compte personnel

original_payload.original_title: ORGEP : Idriss Dokony Adiker dément des transferts vers son compte personnel
original_payload.original_body:
Le général Idriss Dokony Adiker, président de l’Organe de régulation et de gestion du pèlerinage (ORGEP), rejette les accusations de transferts de fonds de l’institution vers son compte bancaire personnel aux Émirats arabes unis. Dans un communiqué signé le 27 novembre 2026, il conteste formellement avoir « effectué, ordonné ou bénéficié » des opérations évoquées.
Son démenti fait référence à une réquisition du procureur général près la cour d’appel de N’Djamena, datée du 23 octobre 2026, prise en exécution d’une ordonnance du président de la Cour suprême. Les accusations qu’il y rapporte portent sur deux transferts présumés de 20 millions et 16,5 millions de dirhams, depuis un compte de l’ORGEP en Arabie saoudite vers son compte à la First Abu Dhabi Bank.
Pour sa défense, Idriss Dokony Adiker explique que le compte saoudien de l’ORGEP, ouvert auprès d’Al Ahli Bank, sert au paiement des prestataires agréés du Hadj. Il soutient que les procédures saoudiennes encadrant ces fonds ne permettent pas à l’institution d’en disposer librement et conteste, sur cette base, la faisabilité des transferts allégués. Il affirme également que le reliquat des fonds de l’exercice 2025 est documenté dans les comptes et le rapport d’audit correspondant.
Un relevé bancaire portant son nom, joint aux documents transmis, affiche un dernier solde de 303 985,20 dirhams. Couvrant la période du 1er septembre au 26 novembre 2026, il ne fait apparaître aucun des deux transferts évoqués. Ce document, limité à cette période, ne permet toutefois pas à lui seul de trancher les accusations.
Le président de l’ORGEP assure n’avoir reçu aucune notification officielle ni demande d’explication de la part des autorités gouvernementales ou de sa hiérarchie. Il se dit disponible pour fournir aux autorités administratives et judiciaires les justificatifs nécessaires et se réserve le droit d’engager des actions pour défendre son honneur.

original_payload.original_title: CEEAC : Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno prend la présidence en exercice, onze ans après son père
original_payload.original_body:
Le Maréchal Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno a officiellement pris, ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026 à Malabo, la présidence en exercice de la Communauté économique des États de l'Afrique centrale (CEEAC). Il succède à son homologue équato-guinéen, Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, à l'issue de la cérémonie de passation de charges.
À la tête de l'organisation régionale, le chef de l'État tchadien hérite d'une institution qui regroupe les pays d'Afrique centrale et dont il devra piloter les grands dossiers : intégration économique, sécurité et coordination entre les États membres. Cette prise de fonction a une résonance particulière pour le Tchad. Son père, le Maréchal Idriss Déby Itno, avait lui aussi exercé cette fonction. Il signait encore, en avril 2013 à N'Djamena, des textes de l'organisation en qualité de président de la CEEAC. Début 2015, il présidait encore, en tant que président en exercice, une concertation à Addis-Abeba. Le relais est passé en 2015, lors d'un sommet à N'Djamena, au président gabonais Ali Bongo Ondimba, qui lui a succédé.
Le Tchad retrouve donc la tête de la CEEAC onze ans après cette passation. C'est aussi la première fois que Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno endosse cette responsabilité, que son père avait occupée avant lui. Dans une région confrontée à des défis sécuritaires et économiques, cette présidence est très attendue. Elle offre à N'Djamena l'occasion de renforcer son rôle de médiateur et de moteur de l'intégration régionale. Reste à voir quelles priorités le nouveau président en exercice fixera pour son mandat.

items.title: Why are families going hungry in northern Yemen even where food is on sale?

original_payload.original_title: Why are families going hungry in northern Yemen even where food is on sale?
original_payload.original_body:
Umm Sami, a widow raising four children in Yemen’s Red Sea port city of Hodeidah, sells household goods and takes on occasional domestic work to feed her family. Rising prices have changed how she shops. “Sometimes we buy a little flour or oil that lasts just one day because we cannot afford a whole bag,” she  told Al Jazeera .
Food is still on the shelves. It was available in the markets that monitors could reach in September, but families had less money to spend, according to the Yemen Joint Monitoring Report, a humanitarian and food security assessment. Across Houthi-controlled areas like Hodeidah, a basket of basic foods cost about 7 percent, or $91, more that month than in August, its highest level in a year.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  How the Houthis fund war effort and tighten grip on Yemen
list 2 of 3  Taiz hospitals near collapse as Houthis tighten siege: Yemen government
list 3 of 3  The escalation in Yemen is a turning point
end of list
Families on both sides of the front lines are struggling, and prices are rising faster in the government-held south, according to the Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET). What sets the Houthi-controlled north apart is how little families there can earn and how little help is left.
Most households in and around northern towns find only five to 10 days of paid work a month, FEWS NET reported in October. The UN World Food Programme’s (WFP) food assistance in Houthi-held areas has been suspended since September 2025, FEWS NET said. By mid-September 2026, WFP had begun a distribution round in government-held areas that aimed to reach about 1.7 million people.
In the last nationwide hunger analysis by UN agencies and their partners, published in mid-2025, the only people projected to face catastrophic hunger, about 41,000, were in four districts of Amran, Hodeidah and Hajjah governorates – all under Houthi control.
original_payload.original_summary: Flour and oil still reach markets in Hodeidah and Sanaa. But high costs and lack of work and aid put it out of reach.
original_payload.author: Al Jazeera Staff

items.title: Venezuela to repeal law that bans opposition figures from office

original_payload.original_title: Venezuela to repeal law that bans opposition figures from office
original_payload.original_body:
Venezuela will repeal a law that prohibits opposition figures from office, National Assembly Chief Jorge Rodriguez has announced.
The legislation, approved in 2024 and criticised for enabling political persecution, targeted those who promoted or supported sanctions against the country.
Recommended Stories

list 2 of 3  Protesters clash with police over Venezuela’s poor minimum wage
list 3 of 3  Argentina bars Central Bank from printing money to fund government spending
end of list
“That law responded to a very specific moment in a particular situation that Venezuela was going through,” Rodriguez said on Thursday.
The law was passed just after fraught elections which the then-incumbent Nicolas Maduro ultimately won amid widespread allegations of fraud.
An interim government headed by Delcy Rodriguez, the parliamentary chief’s sister, has run Venezuela since Maduro’s abduction by US forces in January.  Delcy Rodriguez promised in September  during a speech at the United Nations that the South American country will hold free and fair elections, without setting a date.
Since then, the US-backed government has been in political transition talks with parts of the opposition selected by Washington. That dialogue had reached an agreement to review several laws, including the one up for repeal now, according to Jorge Rodriguez.
Opposition leader Maria Corina Machado shook up Venezuelan politics with her surprise  return from exile last month . Machado won an opposition primary in 2023 to take on Maduro in the following year’s election, but she was legally barred from running. The Nobel Peace Prize laureate is widely expected to run for office in the event of an election, despite her exclusion from transition talks.

items.title: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secrets as AI race heats up

original_payload.original_title: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secrets as AI race heats up
original_payload.original_body:
OpenAI has sued Apple, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching its employees to gain access to its technology.
The ChatGPT maker filed counterclaims in California federal court on Friday, saying that Apple’s employment practices were designed to “trap” employees and prevent them from working on competitors’ technology.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items    list 1 of 4  Apple files lawsuit accusing ChatGPT maker OpenAI of stealing trade secrets
list 2 of 4  John Ternus succeeds Tim Cook as Apple CEO after 15 years
list 3 of 4  Elon Musk’s X Corp and SpaceXAI drop antitrust lawsuit against Apple
list 4 of 4  How AI apps are offering free substitutes for Big Tech software
end of list
OpenAI is developing artificial intelligence-enabled personal electronic devices that threaten to “outcompete Apple on what Apple views as its own turf,” the company said in its Friday court filing.
OpenAI said in the filing that Apple gained confidential information by re-hiring a former employee who worked at OpenAI for six months. In that time, the employee gained access to specific information on a new device as well as OpenAI’s roadmap for future hardware products.
“Given the timing, it now appears that stealing those documents may have been his reason for joining OpenAI in the first place,” OpenAI said.
Apple and OpenAI did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters.
Tensions between the two tech companies have escalated as the intensifying race to develop AI products fuels competition for talent and proprietary technology.

items.title: Israel kills four in Gaza as Hamas chief al-Hayya’s son survives strike

original_payload.original_title: Israel kills four in Gaza as Hamas chief al-Hayya’s son survives strike
original_payload.original_body:
A son of Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya has survived an Israeli air strike targeting his family in Gaza, said the Palestinian group.
The air raid on Friday came as Israeli attacks elsewhere in the strip killed four Palestinians, despite the so-called “ceasefire” agreed over a year ago.
Recommended Stories

list 3 of 3  Why are winter rains forcing Palestinians in Gaza to flee again?

Izzeldeen al-Hayya, 29, and his family survived the Israeli strike at dawn, said Hamas official Basem Naim. Hamas sources told the Reuters news agency that several relatives were wounded, including the daughter-in-law of the Hamas chief.
The family of another of Khalil al-Hayya’s deceased sons, Azzam, also survived.
Naim described Izzeldeen as the Hamas leader’s last surviving son. Four of his brothers were killed by Israeli forces: Hamza in 2008, Osama in 2014, Humam in September last year and Azzam in May this year.
Izzeldeen is the twin brother of Humam, who was killed in an Israeli strike on Hamas leaders in Qatar last year. Khalil al-Hayya narrowly escaped  that attack  during negotiations. He was named leader of Hamas in July.
Hamas condemned Friday’s attack, describing it as an attempt to “assassinate” al-Hayya’s son and target his family.
The group linked the attack to threats made against its leader by Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz and accused Israel of seeking to undermine the October 2025 “ceasefire” agreement. Hamas said the “cowardly act” exposes the “complete detachment from human and moral values” of Israeli leaders.

items.title: Tunisia faces scrutiny over prison deaths as rights groups demand answers on inhumane conditions

original_payload.original_title: Tunisia faces scrutiny over prison deaths as rights groups demand answers on inhumane conditions
original_payload.original_body:
Human Rights
Tunisia's main rights group on Friday denounced "inhumane" conditions in Tunisian prisons, saying 30 inmates have died since the beginning of summer, the country's hottest on record.
Authorities have yet to release figures for prison deaths after a summer marked by multiple heatwaves, water shortages and power cuts. "The situation in prisons is inhumane and catastrophic," said Bassem Trifi, head of the Tunisian League for Human Rights, adding that "overcrowding and the lack of healthcare" in prisons were a major issue.
Tunisian Justice Minister Leila Jaffel said in a parliamentary address last week that some prisons in Tunisia were indeed overcrowded. She also confirmed there were "some deaths" among prisoners, but said that all those who had died had "suffered from chronic illnesses and passed away in hospitals", not in prison.
original_payload.original_summary: Tunisia's main human rights group is sounding the alarm over what it calls inhumane prison conditions, reporting that 30 inmates have died since the start of the country's hottest summer on record.

Family members of five people killed in a fuel tanker accident and local residents gathered outside Al Salam Mosque in Cairo's Waraq district on Friday to bid farewell to the victims. Five members of one family were among those killed- a father, his daughter, his son, and two nephews.
The crash involving a fuel tanker sparked a massive fire on Cairo's Ring Road on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people and injuring at least 21 others, Egyptian authorities said. The blaze, on a major highway encircling the Egyptian capital, left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the Health Ministry.
The crash occurred in Waraq, a densely populated neighborhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area. Rescue workers were seen pulling people from burning vehicles at the scene.

items.title: Paraguay ex-minister arrested over bank collapse

original_payload.original_title: Paraguay ex-minister arrested over bank collapse
original_payload.original_body:
Paraguay’s former economy minister Carlos Fernandez Valdovinos turned himself in on Friday, becoming the latest ex-official placed under arrest following the collapse of one of the country’s largest banks.
The Ueno Bank crisis, which saw millions locked out of their life savings earlier this month, has already prompted the ouster of president Santiago Pena, who has been arrested along with several other former top officials.
An arrest warrant for Valdovinos seen by AFP accused the 61-year-old of “alleged criminal acts of administration for personal gain, aggravated passive bribery, criminal association, and money laundering.”
The public prosecutor’s office alleged that while minister in July 2025, he approved the transfer of tens of millions of dollars in pension fund money to Ueno Bank.
He left office in August, after which he signed a multi-million dollar consulting contract with the business group that controlled Ueno Bank.

items.title: Yayi hails judiciary over victory in Ogun APC governorship case

original_payload.original_title: Yayi hails judiciary over victory in Ogun APC governorship case
original_payload.original_body:
The senator representing Ogun West and the 2027 All Progressives Congress governorship candidate in Ogun State, Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, has commended the judiciary for upholding the rule of law and standing for the truth following a favourable judgment in two suits instituted against his emergence as the APC candidate by Abayomi Semako Hunye, a governorship aspirant in the party.
Justice Okeke of the Federal High Court, Abeokuta, on Friday reportedly dismissed two consolidated suits, FHC/ABJ/CS/1127/2026 and FHC/AB/126/2026, instituted by Hunye against the ruling party, Senator Adeola and the Independent National Electoral Commission, as lacking merit.
In a statement released on Friday by Kayode Odunaro, the media aide to Senator Adeola, the APC governorship candidate expressed satisfaction with the judgment, stressing that the dismissal of the case brought to an end what he described as the plaintiff’s needless pursuit of the matter through media houses and social media trials in a contest in which he scored zero votes.
Adeola said, “I want to commend the Honourable Justice for his erudite judgement in these cases challenging my overwhelming and widely accepted victory in our party primary. I also commend my legal team for their painstaking defense put up during the process. This victory is yet another milestone in our quest for equity and justice in Ogun State 2027 election. To God be the glory once again”.
The senator reportedly said he was unperturbed while the trial lasted, as he was more concerned with galvanising support for his candidacy across the state among stakeholders and launching his 9-Pillar ITESIWAJU Agenda for Ogun State, adding that “with the judicial decision, the coast is now clear for full campaign for the votes of the people”.

Le club breton a retiré jusqu’à nouvel ordre la gestion de l’équipe professionnelle à son entraîneur et à deux adjoints. Sébastien Tambouret, Pierre-Alexandre Lelièvre et Hervé Sekli assurent l’intérim.

Le Stade Rennais a engagé vendredi une procédure à l’encontre de son entraîneur Franck Haise et de ses adjoints Johann Ramaré et Lilian Nalis. Jusqu’à nouvel ordre, la gestion de l’équipe professionnelle est confiée à Sébastien Tambouret, Pierre-Alexandre Lelièvre et Hervé Sekli.
Le  communiqué publié à 20 h 05  ne prononce pas de licenciement et ne fixe pas la durée de cette réorganisation. Haise et ses deux adjoints sont néanmoins écartés de la conduite du groupe pendant la procédure.
Cette décision intervient au lendemain de la défaite rennaise sur le terrain du NEC Nimègue en Ligue Europa. Les Bretons ont perdu 3-1 jeudi soir, après avoir égalisé par Adrien Thomasson à la 36e minute. Deux buts néerlandais inscrits dans les dix dernières minutes ont scellé le résultat.
Franck Haise avait été nommé le 18 février 2026, avec Johann Ramaré et Lilian Nalis, avant de prolonger son contrat d’une saison en août. Le technicien de 54 ans était alors lié au club jusqu’en 2028.
Le trio intérimaire doit désormais préparer le déplacement de Rennes à Toulouse dimanche en Ligue 1. Sébastien Tambouret, habituel entraîneur de la réserve, avait déjà assuré l’intérim de l’équipe première en février entre le départ d’Habib Beye et l’arrivée de Franck Haise.

L’actrice nigériane Adesua Etomi-Wellington a annoncé vendredi 27 novembre qu’un résultat de laboratoire n’avait pas révélé de cancer, au terme de plusieurs mois d’examens médicaux et de visites à l’hôpital.
Dans une vidéo publiée sur Instagram, la comédienne a partagé le moment où elle a informé ses proches du résultat communiqué par son médecin. Elle a présenté cette séquence comme l’issue d’une période marquée par des procédures répétées, des scanners, des injections et des moments d’incertitude.
Adesua Etomi a également expliqué que ces difficultés avaient motivé sa présence plus discrète sur les réseaux sociaux en 2026. Elle a remercié les équipes médicales qui l’ont prise en charge au Nigeria et aux États-Unis, ainsi que ses proches.
L’actrice a notamment salué le soutien de son époux, le chanteur et producteur Banky W, et de leurs enfants. La vidéo montre aussi plusieurs membres de sa famille et des amis célébrant avec elle l’annonce du résultat négatif.
Cette révélation intervient deux jours après la sortie de  On My Way , un titre enregistré par le couple à l’occasion de son neuvième anniversaire de mariage. La chanson doit figurer sur leur album commun  Not Easily Broken , annoncé pour 2027.
La famille avait déjà rendu publiques d’autres épreuves de santé. Banky W avait annoncé en mai 2024 une quatrième intervention liée à un cancer de la peau. Adesua Etomi avait ensuite raconté, en mars 2025, avoir souffert d’hyperémèse gravidique pendant sa deuxième grossesse, avec une hospitalisation puis une césarienne en urgence.

SOMMAIRE
Les échéances de cotisation à respecter
La Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale (CNSS) ne recevra plus aux guichets les demandes d’attestation d’immatriculation et de versement des cotisations à partir du mardi 1er décembre 2026. L’institution a annoncé vendredi 27 novembre la généralisation de la procédure numérique via  service-public.bj .
Pour les employeurs, cette attestation permet de justifier leur immatriculation auprès de la Caisse et le règlement de leurs cotisations. La démarche figure dans le catalogue national des services publics, sous la  référence PS00597 .
Le passage au numérique concerne la manière de demander ces justificatifs. Il ne modifie pas, en lui-même, les obligations de déclaration des salariés et de versement des cotisations qui incombent aux employeurs.
Les échéances de cotisation à respecter
La CNSS distingue deux régimes de périodicité selon l’effectif de l’entreprise. Les employeurs de 20 salariés ou plus règlent leurs cotisations chaque mois, tandis que ceux qui emploient moins de 20 personnes procèdent à un versement trimestriel.
Selon les  modalités publiées par la Caisse , ces sommes doivent être versées dans les quinze jours suivant la fin de la période concernée. Un retard entraîne une majoration de 1,5 % pour chaque mois ou fraction de mois de retard.
La CNSS propose par ailleurs une  attestation destinée aux travailleurs , qui permet à un salarié de s’assurer de son affiliation et du versement de ses cotisations. Le portail affiche un coût de 500 FCFA et un délai indicatif de deux jours pour cette prestation distincte.

MTN a officialisé son offre de paiement en ligne le 26 novembre à Cotonou. Accessible sans carte bancaire physique, le service prévoit des commissions sur les rechargements et les achats.

Partager

SOMMAIRE
Des plafonds distincts de ceux du portefeuille MoMo
Les abonnés de MTN Mobile Money au Bénin peuvent créer une carte virtuelle Mastercard depuis leur téléphone pour payer sur Internet. L’opérateur a lancé officiellement cette offre jeudi 26 novembre, avec Orabank Bénin, qui émet la carte, et Mastercard, qui fournit le réseau de paiement.
La création se fait dans l’application MoMo ou en composant le code *880#, à condition de disposer d’un portefeuille actif et correctement identifié. Le client reçoit des identifiants de carte utilisables sur les sites marchands qui acceptent les cartes prépayées Mastercard. Il peut ensuite alimenter la carte à partir du portefeuille électronique, sans ouvrir un compte bancaire supplémentaire pour cette démarche.
L’émission coûte 500 FCFA. Selon la grille présentée lors du lancement, chaque rechargement est facturé à 0,5 % et chaque achat à 1,5 %. Un paiement de 10 000 FCFA entraîne donc une commission de 150 FCFA, sans compter les frais de rechargement et les éventuels frais liés au change pour un achat en devises.
Des plafonds distincts de ceux du portefeuille MoMo
La carte est valable un an, ne permet pas d’emprunter et son solde ne peut excéder 2 millions de FCFA. Les transactions et rechargements sont soumis à un plafond cumulé mensuel de 10 millions de FCFA, d’après les conditions communiquées au lancement.
Ces limites sont différentes de celles du portefeuille MoMo lui-même. Depuis le 2 novembre,  le plafond de solde du compte MoMo est passé à 4 millions de FCFA . Les transferts nationaux via PI-SPI bénéficient par ailleurs d’une franchise quotidienne jusqu’à 8 000 FCFA, une règle qui ne concerne pas les achats réglés par carte.
Orabank avait annoncé le 18 septembre la disponibilité de la carte dans l’application de MTN. Au lancement officiel, le directeur général de MTN Mobile Money Bénin, Serge Soglo, a indiqué que plus de 200 000 cartes avaient été émises pendant la phase pilote. L’opérateur vise désormais plus d’un million de cartes.
Le titulaire peut consulter ses opérations et bloquer sa carte depuis les canaux MoMo. L’opérateur présente notamment sur  sa page dédiée au service  les abonnements numériques et les achats sur les plateformes en ligne parmi les usages de cette carte.

items.title: IGAD Lauds Pulse of Africa for Amplifying Human Mobility Stories Across Horn of Africa

original_payload.original_title: IGAD Lauds Pulse of Africa for Amplifying Human Mobility Stories Across Horn of Africa
original_payload.original_body:
Addis Ababa, November 27, 2026 (ENA)— The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) has commended Pulse of Africa (POA), an Addis Ababa-based Pan-African media platform, for its valuable media partnership and extensive coverage of regional issues, particularly human mobility and the 2026 IGAD Media Awards.
In a special message of appreciation shared on its social media platforms, the IGAD Secretariat described Pulse of Africa as a valued media partner, thanking the outlet for its contribution to amplifying important stories across the region.
“A special thank you to Pulse of Africa, our valued Media Partner!” the Secretariat stated.
IGAD further recognized POA's extensive coverage of the fourth edition of the IGAD Media Awards, held in Kampala, Uganda, last week.
The Pulse of Africa’s support helped celebrate and recognize outstanding journalists and digital storytellers from across the region, the statement noted.
“Your invaluable support helped us celebrate and recognise outstanding journalists and digital storytellers from across the IGAD region whose work shines a light on free movement of persons, labour migration, human mobility and displacement,” the Secretariat said.
The recognition underscores Pulse of Africa's growing contribution to regional journalism, particularly its reporting on human mobility dynamics in the Greater Horn of Africa, a region facing complex challenges and opportunities related to migration, displacement, refugee protection and cross-border movement.
The IGAD region is currently home to approximately 5.6 million refugees, making informed reporting and public awareness of human mobility issues increasingly important to regional cooperation and policy discussions.
Through its regional reporting, POA has been amplifying the experiences of displaced communities, migration-related developments and broader efforts to advance safe, orderly and regular human mobility across the region.
Its extensive coverage of the 2026 IGAD Media Awards also brought greater visibility to journalists and digital storytellers whose work is helping shape public understanding of free movement, labour migration and displacement across the Greater Horn of Africa.
The fourth edition of the awards recognized approximately 20 outstanding journalists and storytellers for their contributions to journalism and digital storytelling, highlighting the media's role in informing public debate and transforming narratives across the region.
IGAD also praised Pulse of Africa for its continued efforts to amplify stories that matter to communities across the region.
“Thank you for being part of this remarkable journey and for your continued commitment to amplifying the stories that matter across our region,” the Secretariat added.
The commendation further highlights the importance of media partnerships in strengthening regional awareness, promoting informed public discourse and bringing African stories and perspectives to wider audiences.

items.title: New satellite data shows how fast some African cities are sinking

original_payload.original_title: New satellite data shows how fast some African cities are sinking
original_payload.original_body:
New satellite data shows how fast some African cities are sinking
Image source,  Getty Images
Image caption,    Four million people in Lagos, Nigeria may be exposed to extreme sea levels by the end of the century, a new study says
By  Alex Brian   Climate and Science reporter
Published
3 hours ago
Some of Africa's largest cities are sinking faster than previously thought, new research shows.
Scientists used radar imagery from the European Space Agency's Sentinel-1 satellites to map how much the land beneath 20 African coastal cities had moved.
The study found that some cities - including Lagos in Nigeria and Alexandria in Egypt - were sinking much faster than previously estimated in 2021 by the UN's climate body, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC).
While some causes of this sinking, or subsidence, are natural, many are the result of human activities, such as the extraction of groundwater from underneath the Earth's surface.
Lead author Oluwaseyi Dasho said the effects of subsidence "are often invisible in everyday life, but over decades they can substantially increase flood exposure".
This is because when the ground sinks it becomes lower relative to the ocean and adds to the risk of the  sea level rises caused by climate change .
Seven million people, one billion buildings and $180bn (£137bn) of assets could be at flood risk by 2050, the paper estimated.
Satellites give a clearer picture
In the past, a lack of monitoring stations has prevented scientists from obtaining up-to-date localised information on subsidence in Africa, Dasho said.
But by using satellite data, the researchers from Virginia Tech were able to detect land movements as small as 1mm per year.
Senior author Manoochehr Shirzaei said  Sentinel-1 satellites  flew over the same region of the Earth every six to 12 days.
"[The satellite] transmits the radar signal, which hits the ground and bounces back to the satellite," the geosciences professor explained. This process is then repeated on "many revisits".
The time between sending the signal and receiving it back is recorded, with changes in this value over time revealing how much the land has moved.
Image source,  Getty Images
Image caption,    More of Alexandria could be exposed to flooding than previously thought, the research says
The ground under Alexandria and Lagos was found to have sunk an average of 6mm and 5mm per year respectively.
If this rate continued, sea levels around Alexandria would rise 36% more by 2050 than  the IPCC predicted ,  external  , under the middle estimates for how much planet-warming emissions will increase.
Luanda in Angola has also sunk significantly, but other cities such as Durban in South Africa have remained stable or even risen slightly.
Shirzaei said showing where the IPCC had underestimated risks - but also where the threat had been overestimated - could help planners allocate resources more effectively.
Sinking caused by local activities
The man-made drivers of subsidence are usually "extremely local, [which] means that we can combat them by creating local policies", Shirzaei explained.
One major cause is the  increased water consumption  of rapidly growing cities. Too much water being extracted from the ground can lead to the soil becoming compacted and the surface sinking.
The Aswan Dam on the Nile may also be trapping sediment upstream and preventing the replacement of sinking land in Alexandria, the study suggests.
In Lagos, the reclaiming of land from the ocean to create artificial islands and the construction of buildings on loose ground are other possible causes of subsidence.
Why are some cities sinking?
Hear from those trying to solve the problem
Listen on Sounds
Methods of preventing cities from sinking include supplying other water sources and growing less water-intensive crops.
"Whatever we cannot mitigate, we try to adapt to it," Shirzaei added. This could mean  building flood defences or moving key infrastructure to a higher level .
The professor said developing countries had been "left out" of much of the planning for sea-level rises due to a lack of monitoring.
The techniques developed in this study could potentially be used to address the knowledge gap in other regions, such as the Pacific islands, Shirzaei suggested.
Oluwaseyi Dasho said he hoped  the paper, in Science Advances, ,  external   could help African governments "prepare adequately for future challenges and more importantly for the future generations".

items.title: Kenyan cult leader guilty of manslaughter more than 123 starvation deaths

original_payload.original_title: Kenyan cult leader guilty of manslaughter more than 123 starvation deaths
original_payload.original_body:
A Kenyan court has found cult leader Paul Mackenzie guilty of manslaughter over the deaths of 123 of his followers, the latest conviction for Mackenzie, the founder and pastor of the Good News International Church.
Mackenzie was convicted on Friday in the coastal city of Mombasa, along with 29 followers, including his wife, Rhoda Mumbua.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items    list 1 of 4  Is this ancient Swahili town at risk from Kenya’s energy boom
list 2 of 4  Kenya’s growing doping crisis overshadows legacy as athletics powerhouse
list 3 of 4  Kenya’s internet metering bill raises privacy and affordability concerns
list 4 of 4  Kenya gov’t violated constitution with Ebola quarantine site, court says
end of list
Magistrate Alex Ithuku said Mackenzie “gave the directions to fast to death”, Reuters reported. Mackenzie pleaded not guilty, and one of his lawyers said he would appeal after sentencing.
Earlier convictions
On November 6, Mackenzie was sentenced to  200 years in prison  for the murder of 191 people, 190 of them children. He had denied forcing the victims to starve, but the court rejected his defence.
He was also convicted this week of child cruelty, assault, radicalisation and “terrorism-related offences”, according to Reuters. He is due to be sentenced on the child cruelty and radicalisation charges in December, The Associated Press reported.
The Shakahola deaths
Mackenzie led the Good News International Church in the Shakahola Forest, near Kenya’s Indian Ocean coast.
He told followers to starve themselves and their children to death to meet Jesus before the end of the world.
Police arrested him in 2023 after a tip-off, and authorities began uncovering  more than 400 bodies . People familiar with the cult told Reuters that Mackenzie planned the starvation in  three phases : children first, then women and young men, and finally, the remaining men.
Mackenzie had been arrested twice before, in connection with the deaths of children, and released.

items.title: Africa: COP31 - Is Article 6 Delivering Climate Finance?

original_payload.original_title: Africa: COP31 - Is Article 6 Delivering Climate Finance?
original_payload.original_body:
Global carbon markets have built much of the infrastructure needed to finance emission reductions, yet adaptation still depends heavily on shrinking official development assistance (ODA) from public sources. That imbalance was the focus of an African Development Bank (AfDB) event at the Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs) Pavilion during the 2026 UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, on 11 November 2026.
The question on the table was whether Article 6 of the Paris Agreement is delivering the finance expected of it. Country representatives, MDBs and private-sector panellists concluded that markets under Articles 6.2 and 6.4 are gaining momentum but have yet to reach the required scale. Article 6.8 non-market approaches, including the Adaptation Benefits Mechanism (ABM), could help close the adaptation finance gap.
Moderating the discussion, Luc Gnacadja, Mayor of Cotonou, Gold Standard Board member, and Co-Chair of the ABM Executive Committee, framed the challenge clearly: the Paris Agreement set climate action on two legs, mitigation and adaptation, yet a decade later, markets largely support only mitigation.
From policy readiness to bankable projects
Dmitry Halubouski, Principal, Climate Strategy and Delivery at the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), said Article 6 infrastructure and demand were expanding, with more bilateral agreements being established and many countries incorporating carbon-markets cooperation into their Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).
However, he cautioned that agreements alone did not generate finance, and the priority is to convert policy readiness into bankable transactions.
The EBRD is already combining results-based, non-debt carbon finance with conventional lending. In Tunisia, monetising part of the emission reductions through Japan's Joint Crediting Mechanism safeguarded two renewable-energy projects against rising costs, while the country retained credits for its own targets. MDBs are also moving towards country platforms that aggregate projects, employ digital monitoring, and blend concessional finance with carbon revenues.
Muyi Kazeem and Laurence Ibhafidon of Triple E Systems outlined AfDB-supported efforts to strengthen Article 6 readiness across Africa. Since 2021, the focus has shifted from foundational knowledge to practical projects, including pilots in Ghana and Benin. Developers still face high early-stage costs, and many national authorities lack the capacity to assess proposals. Through the AfDB-Korea partnership, funded by the Korea-Africa Economic Cooperation (KOAFEC) Trust Fund, 17 guidelines and templates are being finalised to guide countries and developers from project origination to credit issuance.
Adaptation projects face a different problem. Gareth Phillips, AfDB Manager for Climate and Environment Finance, said projects delivering resilience, biodiversity and nature benefits often lack the predictable revenues needed to service commercial debt.
The ABM addresses this constraint under Article 6.8. Following approved methodologies, validation and verification, it issues non-tradable Certified Adaptation Benefits (CABs) based on project-specific resilience outputs or outcomes that are highly likely to deliver long-term impact.
CABs have three defining features. First, they are non-fungible and unsuitable for speculation because adaptation benefits reflect local needs. Second, their price is determined by the project's financing gap; issuance stops once that barrier is overcome, applying the same minimum-concessionality principles used by MDBs and climate funds. Third, CABs can crowd in capital through forward-sale contracts that support commercial borrowing or be sold ex post to replenish grants and recycle scarce public finance.

original_payload.original_body:
Afrique du Sud: malgré son revers aux municipales, l'ANC garde les grandes villes grâce à des coalitions
Trois semaines après les élections municipales, on connaît désormais la composition de tous les conseils municipaux, le nom des maires et les différentes ententes entre partis en Afrique du Sud. Dans un paysage politique fracturé, la plupart des villes sud-africaines sont désormais dirigées par des coalitions. C'est ainsi que le parti de Nelson Mandela, affaibli après avoir enregistré son pire score électoral – à peine plus de 30% –, reste tout de même au pouvoir dans la plupart des grandes villes, dont Johannesburg, mais perd le poste de maire.

Fikile Mbalula, membre de l'African National Congress (ANC), salue Cyril Ramaphosa, président de l'Afrique du Sud et dirigeant de l'ANC, lors d'une réunion visant à définir la stratégie à adopter dans le cadre des négociations de coalition à la suite des élections municipales, à Johannesburg, en Afrique du Sud, le 12 novembre 2026.        © REUTERS/Oupa Nkosi/File Photo
Par :
RFI
Publicité
Avec notre correspondant à Johannesburg ,  Valentin Hugues
Même si le Congrès national africain (ANC) reste le premier parti du pays,   pas question de parler de victoire  , rappelle son secrétaire général, Fikile Mbalula. «  Nous avons entendu le message des communautés dans lesquelles l'adhésion à l'ANC a reculé. Leur jugement doit guider notre travail de renouvellement , assure-t-il.  La confiance avec laquelle nous abordons ce nouveau mandat s'accompagne donc d'une détermination tout aussi forte à corriger nos faiblesses qu'à rétablir la confiance du public.  »
Face à la déroute, le comité exécutif de l'ANC s'est réuni plusieurs fois ces trois dernières semaines. Et le parti a parfois eu   beaucoup de mal à se mettre d'accord  , notamment sur la question de faire équipe ou non avec l'Alliance démocratique (DA), deuxième parti du pays et principal adversaire de l'ANC.
«  L'ANC et la DA sont les deux principaux partis du pays. Dans ce contexte, nous avons décidé de travailler avec eux uniquement quand il n'y a pas d'autre option. Cette politique du  ''DA comme dernier recours''  est une résolution de notre Conseil général, et le Comité exécutif national n'a fait que la mettre en œuvre  », ajoute Fikile Mbalula.
Les voix de l'ANC ne se reportent pas seulement vers la DA, mais aussi vers des formations plus populistes comme ActionSA, qui récupère le poste de maire à Johannesburg. Ou vers le MK, dirigé par l'ancien président   Jacob Zuma   depuis son exclusion de l'ANC. Son parti prend les rênes de Durban, troisième ville d'  Afrique du Sud  .

items.title: Patrimoine: au Cameroun, le traditionnel medzang fait toujours danser [2/2]

original_payload.original_title: Patrimoine: au Cameroun, le traditionnel medzang fait toujours danser [2/2]
original_payload.original_body:
Reportage Afrique
Patrimoine: au Cameroun, le traditionnel medzang fait toujours danser [2/2]
Publié le :  28/11/2026 - 00:10
Écouter - 02:57
Suite et fin de notre série au Cameroun sur les défenseurs du patrimoine culturel. Aujourd'hui, place au medzang. Ce terme désigne les balafons chez les Fang Bulu-Béti, un groupe culturel de près de six millions d'habitants. Longtemps réservé aux rites et aux fêtes de village, ce rythme a conquis les cabarets urbains, notamment grâce au célèbre Richard Band de Zoetele. À Yaoundé, la tradition fait toujours danser.
Le balafon, encore appelé le medzang, à Yaoundé le 5 novembre 2026.        © Emmanuel Jules Ntap / RFI
Publicité
Sous les ovations, Akim Kondor entre en scène. C'est l'une des figures majeures du medzang au   Cameroun  . «  Avant, on jouait le medzang uniquement dans les villages   ; c'est moi qui ai contribué à faire connaître le medzang à Yaoundé et à Douala  », explique-t-il.
Quarante-cinq ans de carrière, commencée à l'âge de six ans. Aujourd'hui, le musicien forme la relève, mais déplore le manque de moyens : «  On n'a pas de soutien, on ne parvient pas à trouver des promoteurs qui peuvent nous aider à évoluer plus et à mettre le balafon au niveau international . »
Qu'importe, il enchaîne les scènes. Ce soir, c'est dans un cabaret d'Ahala, au sud de Yaoundé. Parmi les habitués, Mélanie Yalla, une sexagénaire en joie à l'idée de revivre les souvenirs d'enfance. «  Je trouve que ce concept, c'est pour promouvoir nos valeurs afin que nos enfants et petits-fils ne perdent pas leurs repères  », affirme-t-elle.
À lire aussi  Le balafon, une histoire d'héritage
La nuit avance, et la piste attire aussi la jeunesse, à l'image de Thomas Delors Nti. «  Ce sont mes amis qui m'ont invité à venir suivre au medzang. C'est une musique intemporelle et ceux qui chantent étalent tout leur talent  », raconte-t-il.
Ce son acoustique si particulier vient d'un savoir-faire ancestral, explique l'historien de l'art Marc Okali : «  Il y a des spécialistes fabricants de balafons, de medzangs non loin de Yaoundé, dans la localité d'Okali. Cet instrument est fabriqué à partir d'un arbre dont le bois est rouge, son nom commercial est le padouk. Cet arbre vibre et a des sonorités spéciales.  »
Les lames de bois rouge reposent sur des calebasses, qui servent de caisses de résonance. Frappées par deux baguettes, elles offrent une architecture musicale complète. «  Quand vous observez le balafon, il y a la solo, l'accompagnement et la basse comme avec tous les autres instruments modernes  », ajoute Akim Kondor. Et dès que les voix des chanteuses s'élèvent, le cabaret tout entier entre dans la danse.

items.title: NMDPRA tasks lubricant producers on compliance, warns against substandard products

original_payload.original_title: NMDPRA tasks lubricant producers on compliance, warns against substandard products
original_payload.original_body:
Oil & Gas  NMDPRA tasks lubricant producers on compliance, warns against substandard products
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   10 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Joy Akinsanya
The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) has urged lubricant manufacturers and blending plant operators in Ogun to comply with regulatory standards, ensure product quality and prioritise operational safety.
The state coordinator, Akinyemi Atilola, said this at a stakeholders’ engagement on lubricant oil and blending plant operations held on Thursday in Abeokuta.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the programme has the theme: “Advancing the Growth and Sustainability of Lube Oil and Blending Plant Operations in Ogun State Through Effective Regulatory Frameworks”.
Atilola described operators in the lubricant industry as critical contributors to economic growth, noting that their businesses supported households through employment and other economic activities.
He said the authority recognised stakeholders’ investments and would not adopt an approach that unnecessarily frustrate businesses, stressing its commitment to facilitating investment and sustainable growth.
Atilola, however.  cautioned operators against compromising standards, warning that unsafe operations, poor quality products and disregard for regulatory requirements could undermine investments and damage business reputations.
“We are not just a regulator. We are business enablers. We enable your business and make sure that it grows.
“The authority is introducing a more responsive regulatory approach under Project Nexus, designed to promote prompt service delivery, fairness and collaboration with industry operators,” he said.
Atilola promised that companies submitting applications to the authority would receive responses within 24 hours, adding that applications would be treated fairly to prevent avoidable administrative delays.
He said the authority would also consider advancing applications to subsequent stages where outstanding documents could be submitted later, provided the circumstances permitted such consideration.
The NMDPRA coordinator also warned against illegal and unsafe petroleum operations, citing the inspection of an illegal refinery in Ogun where equipment and materials were substandard.
He said the facility posed environmental and safety risks, saying that operators must comply with applicable standards to protect their investments and the public.
Highlighting the state’s industrial potential, Atilola said the concentration of manufacturing industries and demand for lubricants used in vehicles and machinery presented opportunities across the industry’s value chain.
In a technical presentation, the Head of Operations, NMDPRA Abeokuta Field Office, Mr Femi Adebowale, urged lubricant manufacturers to maintain accurate production records.
He warned that discrepancies between raw material inputs, production volumes and products supplied to customers could undermine regulatory reconciliation exercises.
Adebowale warned against using unverified base oil and additives, incorrect blending ratios, contamination and unauthorised changes to product formulations.
He explained that product certification by the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) does not replace operational approvals required from the NMDPRA.
He also urged operators to report suspected counterfeit and substandard lubricants to the authority.
A participant, Mr Tunde Lawani, Secretary of the Association of Lubricant Third-Party Blenders, commended the NMDPRA for organising the engagement.
“Participants already gained valuable knowledge on the need for third party blenders to establish proper operational structures, adhere to quality standards and ensure full regulatory compliance. (NAN)

original_payload.original_body:
Health  Foundation, NIMR to partner on health research, specialist training
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   10 hours ago   ·  2 min read
✓
✓
By Oluwafunke Ishola
The Tunji Olowolafe Foundation (TOF) says it will partner with the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR) to strengthen health research, specialist medical training and healthcare delivery across Nigeria.
The foundation’s founder, Dr Tunji Olowolafe, made the commitment on Thursday at the 2026 NIMR Annual International Scientific Conference in Lagos, where he served as Chairman of the Conference.
Olowolafe, Chancellor of Ekiti State University, said the proposed partnership would explore areas of mutual interest, including health research, healthcare infrastructure, specialist training and improved access to quality medical services.
He said the collaboration would provide an opportunity to connect the foundation’s healthcare interventions with NIMR’s research expertise to develop practical solutions to the country’s health challenges.
Olowolafe said NIMR was mandated to investigate health problems of national importance and generate scientific evidence to improve healthcare delivery and strengthen public health systems.
Commending the institute’s contributions during the Ebola and COVID-19 outbreaks, he emphasised the need to strengthen research infrastructure and build indigenous capacity to address emerging health challenges.
He said the foundation had supported several healthcare initiatives, including the Gbemisola Olowolafe Centre for Ophthalmic Simulation (GOCOS) at the Guinness Eye Centre, Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH).
He said the centre was established in partnership with the Faculty of Ophthalmology of the National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria and commissioned in 2026.
He said that the centre housed a Haag-Streit Eyesi Surgical Simulator, which allowed ophthalmology residents and surgeons to practise surgical procedures virtually before performing operations on patients.
Olowolafe said the foundation had also contributed to infrastructural development at the Lagos State University College of Medicine (LASUCOM).
He added that TOF supported grassroots primary healthcare initiatives in Are-Ekiti, Ekiti State, focusing on maternal care, routine immunisation and community-based healthcare services.
“Our interventions also include digital health solutions to improve access to healthcare in underserved communities,” he said.
He called for stronger collaboration among research institutions, industry and other stakeholders to translate scientific discoveries into practical solutions that would improve healthcare outcomes.
Olowolafe also emphasised the need for Nigeria to strengthen its domestic vaccine production capacity and preparedness against emerging health threats through sustained investment in research and local scientific capabilities.(NAN)

items.title: Nigeria, Togo target $50m data park investment

original_payload.original_title: Nigeria, Togo target $50m data park investment
original_payload.original_body:
Science & Tech  Nigeria, Togo target $50m data park investment
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   5 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
​‌‌⁠‌⁠‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​‍​‍‍‍​‌​
By Stellamaris Ashinze and Kunle Williams
Nigeria and Togo are targeting an initial investment of between $30 million and $50 million to establish a joint data park.
The Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Dr Bosun Tijani, disclosed this on Thursday at the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding in Lagos.
Tijani said the Nigeria-Togo Twin Data Park initiative would be structured as a joint Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV), involving government and private sector investments.
He said both countries were targeting initial project milestones by the second quarter of 2027, subject to funding and transaction processes.
According to him, Nigeria has identified Egbin in Lagos State as its proposed location, while Togo is finalising its preferred site.
“Egbin was selected for its proximity to the Egbin Power Plant, water resources, gas supply, connectivity and security.
“The location’s access to electricity and gas infrastructure would support reliable power supply, while water would facilitate cooling operations,” he said.
Tijani said the initiative would provide dedicated infrastructure for data centre operators rather than involve governments directly constructing data centres.
He said governments would provide equity, regulatory support and enabling legislation, while private investors would contribute substantial funding and participate in management.
The minister said the proposed park would serve Nigeria, Togo and other West African countries, covering both Francophone and Anglophone markets.
He added that the partnership could attract global data centre operators seeking opportunities in Africa’s expanding digital economy.
Tijani said locating data centres closer to users would reduce latency, improve digital service delivery and strengthen regional data infrastructure.
According to him, Nigeria’s data consumption reached 1.7 million terabytes in August 2026, compared with about 400,000 terabytes five years earlier.
He added that Nigeria’s data centre capacity, measured in megawatts, increased by 65 per cent between 2024 and 2025.
Tijani said the initiative would complement Nigeria’s planned 90,000-kilometre fibre-optic network and investments in 3,700 telecommunications towers across underserved communities.
On data sovereignty, the minister said Nigeria was exploring a data embassy framework allowing other countries to host critical data within designated facilities.
He explained that the arrangement would provide legal safeguards preventing host countries from unilaterally determining how participating countries’ data would be managed.
Tijani said Nigeria’s cloud policy and strengthened data protection regulations would provide the foundation for attracting investments and safeguarding information.
He added that the initiative aligned with Nigeria’s ambition to attract about $750 million in cloud investments under its national cloud policy.
Meanwhile, Togo’s Minister for Digital Economy and Transformation, Ms Cina Lawson, described the initiative as the first joint digital infrastructure project between both countries.
Lawson said Togo was expanding fibre connectivity to 2,700 schools, 250 hospitals and all districts under its digital development programme.
She said the partnership would make Togo more attractive to international data centre operators that might otherwise favour larger markets.
According to her, the initiative would enable both countries to attract investors serving English-speaking and French-speaking markets across West Africa.
Lawson said both countries would collaborate with the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) to develop regulations supporting the initiative.
She added that the proposed framework would allow participating countries to establish data centres within the parks under agreed legal arrangements. (NAN)
Edited by Kamal Tayo Oropo

items.title: Thousands of Puerto Ricans join ‘Day of National Outrage’ protest

original_payload.original_title: Thousands of Puerto Ricans join ‘Day of National Outrage’ protest
original_payload.original_body:
Thousands of Puerto Ricans have protested in the capital, San Juan, as anger and frustration erupted over record-high electricity rates, the surging cost of living, deteriorating basic services and other issues.
Retirees, university students, bus drivers and others joined Friday’s protest organised by some 30 groups ranging from unions to religious organisations. The crowds gathered in front of a mall for what organisers dubbed the “Day of National Outrage”.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  Young French students who see ‘no change’ keep up protests in Paris suburbs
list 2 of 3  Anti-austerity strike spurs transport chaos across Belgium
list 3 of 3  Protesting Bangladesh garment workers reject pay offer
end of list
Hundreds of demonstrators arrived by bus in San Juan from dozens of cities and towns across the island.
Asked what problems Puerto Rico had, 74-year-old Radames Garcia Badillo said: “Where to start? The outrage is absolute.”
He said that power and water services are unreliable and that his neighbourhood goes dark at least once a week for several hours. He also decried a sharp increase in the cost of living.
“We’re buying less because things are extremely expensive,” he said. “For us retirees, it is essential to make every dollar stretch.”
The protest, one of the largest in the US territory since Governor Jenniffer Gonzalez took office in January 2025, grew throughout the day as demonstrators took over one of the island’s main highways, forcing its closure.
Organisers estimated that some 8,000 people took part, according to local media.
Many in the crowd waved or wore the Puerto Rican flag. Some chose the flag from before the island became a US commonwealth in 1952, often a sign of cultural pride and sometimes of resistance.
Soaring electricity bills
“Things have never been good in Puerto Rico, but they keep getting worse,” said Veronica Ishtar, a visual arts student.

items.title: At least eight found dead on migrant boat off Spain’s Canary Islands

original_payload.original_title: At least eight found dead on migrant boat off Spain’s Canary Islands
original_payload.original_body:
At least eight migrants have been found dead on a boat carrying about 100 people that was rescued near Spain’s Canary Islands, the Spanish maritime rescue service has said.
The rescue service said on Friday that between eight and 10 bodies were found on board and that six people were airlifted to hospital in serious condition.

list 3 of 3  What Spain’s election means for Morocco

The boat was found 39 nautical miles (72km) south of the island of El Hierro and was being towed to the port of La Estaca.
Separately, 84 survivors from another boat came ashore at La Restinga, El Hierro’s main port, which has a reception centre and field hospital for migrants.
The Canary Islands are a Spanish region in the Atlantic Ocean, off the coast of northwest Africa. Anyone who lands there reaches Spanish and European Union territory, which has made the islands a main entry point for migrants from West Africa.
Arrivals hit a record of more than 46,000 in 2024 before falling after tighter surveillance and cooperation with countries of origin and transit.
Patrols off Senegal, Mauritania and Morocco have pushed departures further south to The Gambia, Guinea-Bissau and Guinea, making the crossing longer and more dangerous.
Record arrivals
Arrivals in the Canary Islands have accelerated since October, with a record 2,100 people reaching the islands in a single day earlier this week, mostly on El Hierro, which has 11,400 residents.
Authorities there  declared an emergency  earlier this month, and rescuers brought in  nearly 1,500 people in a single day  on November 14.

items.title: Will Taiwan vote to revive nuclear power – and why does that matter for AI?

original_payload.original_title: Will Taiwan vote to revive nuclear power – and why does that matter for AI?
original_payload.original_body:
Voters in Taiwan are set to decide whether to bring back nuclear power – 18 months after its last operational reactor was shut down.
A referendum on the issue is being held alongside local elections on Saturday. It is the island’s fourth vote on nuclear power in just eight years.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  Xi Jinping says Taiwan’s ‘complete reunification’ with China will happen
list 2 of 3  Asian stock markets tumble as AI bubble fears mount
list 3 of 3  Asia’s markets dive as return of Nvidia’s Huang fails to quell AI doubts
end of list
It comes as demand for electricity to fuel the country’s burgeoning computer chip industry soars and concern grows about how Taiwan would keep its lights on if China, which claims the island as its own territory, cut it off amid escalating tensions.
Here is what we know.
What is the referendum about?
Voters are being asked whether the government should return to using nuclear power to boost the economy. That would mean abolishing the country’s longstanding “nuclear-free homeland” policy.
The opposition Kuomintang (KMT) proposed the referendum and the Taiwan People’s Party (TPP) is also backing it. The legislature approved the referendum in August and the Central Election Commission signed it off on August 28.
To pass, ‘yes’ votes must outnumber ‘no’ votes and exceed a quarter of all eligible voters.
The ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), which has long had a policy of no nuclear power in its mandate, is urging ‘no’. DPP legislator Chen Pei-yu called the referendum unnecessary, saying lawmakers could change the policy by amending existing laws instead.
Why did Taiwan give up nuclear power?
Taiwan once relied heavily on nuclear power. In 1985, its three plants produced 52 percent of the nation’s electricity.

The latest figures released by the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission on Friday showed that the 11 distribution companies recorded an 82.39 per cent collection efficiency in September, down from 84.62 per cent in August—a decline of 2.23 percentage points.

items.title: What happens to unused embryos after IVF?

original_payload.original_title: What happens to unused embryos after IVF?
original_payload.original_body:
Imagine that after years of struggling to have a child, you finally achieve your dream through in vitro fertilisation. Your joy is overwhelming, but there is something you may not immediately think about. Several embryos created during your IVF treatment may still be frozen in a laboratory, waiting for a decision about their future.
Perhaps you intend to return for another child, or perhaps you have already had the number of children you want; you may even have changed your mind about having another pregnancy. Whatever your circumstances, those embryos remain in storage, and someone must eventually decide what happens to them.
This is one of the less discussed consequences of modern fertility treatment. While much attention is given to the success of IVF, the fate of embryos that are never transferred is often overlooked. When you begin IVF, your immediate concern is understandably getting pregnant.
You may not want to imagine a situation in which you have more embryos than you need, or find yourself making decisions about them years after your treatment. Yet that is precisely the dilemma confronting many couples who undergo assisted reproductive treatment.

items.title: Payaza repays N88.94bn CP to Nigerian investors, expands operations

original_payload.original_title: Payaza repays N88.94bn CP to Nigerian investors, expands operations
original_payload.original_body:
Payaza Africa Limited, a pan-African payments infrastructure company, has successfully repaid N88.94bn (approximately $65 million) to investors under its commercial paper programme listed on Nigeria’s FMDQ Securities Exchange.
The repayment comes weeks after the Central Bank of Kenya authorised the company to provide payment gateway services under the country’s National Payment System Act, 2011. The authorisation enables Payaza to provide payment services directly to Kenyan businesses, including online checkout solutions and payment processing through bank cards, mobile money and bank transfers.
In a statement on Friday, the company highlighted its successful repayment of N88.94bn to Nigerian investors as evidence of its financial discipline and commitment to meeting its obligations.
“Commercial paper is short-term debt raised from institutional investors, and every issue carries a fixed date on which the money must be paid back. Repaying it on schedule is one of the plainest public tests of a company’s liquidity and discipline,” the statement added.

SOMMAIRE
Des investissements engagés avant le nouvel accord
Le directeur général de Sonatel, Brelotte Ba, a annoncé vendredi 27 novembre que les investissements de l’opérateur dans ses réseaux dépasseraient 600 milliards de FCFA à l’horizon 2030. L’annonce est intervenue à l’issue de la première réunion du comité de suivi du partenariat conclu avec l’État sénégalais pour accompagner sa stratégie numérique.
Le programme commun porte sur 16 des 63 projets du New Deal technologique. Il prévoit notamment de faciliter les échanges de données entre administrations, de développer les paiements électroniques et de renforcer la sécurité informatique. La signature électronique et l’hébergement des données figurent également parmi les domaines retenus. Le partenariat, prévu pour trois ans, n’est pas exclusif.
La diffusion des services reste un enjeu distinct de la construction des réseaux. Selon Brelotte Ba, la couverture 4G atteint 98 % de la population du Sénégal, alors qu’environ la moitié de celle-ci utilise effectivement cette technologie.
Des investissements engagés avant le nouvel accord
Dans son  communiqué du 9 juillet 2026 , Sonatel avait annoncé la mise en place de 16 antennes satellites supplémentaires sur le site de Gandoul avec Eutelsat OneWeb. Cette infrastructure permet de relier les réseaux terrestres aux satellites en orbite basse. Le groupe avait également déclaré, dans ses résultats semestriels de juillet, viser le raccordement de 1,3 million de foyers à la fibre au Sénégal à la fin de 2026.
L’effort d’investissement s’inscrit dans une stratégie nationale lancée par le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye le 24 février 2025. Parmi les mesures alors présentées figurent une identité numérique fondée sur la biométrie et un portail unique donnant accès aux démarches administratives. Le ministre des Télécommunications et du Numérique, Samba Diouf, a annoncé vendredi un suivi continu des projets. Les services chargés des finances et de la régulation de la commande publique seront associés aux travaux sur les investissements.

items.title: Ormuz : la raffinerie Dangote, grande gagnante africaine de la crise

original_payload.original_title: Ormuz : la raffinerie Dangote, grande gagnante africaine de la crise
original_payload.original_body:
Photo : DR
Ormuz : la raffinerie Dangote, grande gagnante africaine de la crise
27/11/2026    par    Francis Noude
Facebook  Twitter  WhatsApp
La raffinerie  Dangote , installée près de  Lagos  au  Nigeria , a expédié 561 000 barils de produits pétroliers par jour au deuxième trimestre 2026, contre 79 000 en moyenne en 2023, d’après une  analyse de l’Agence américaine d’information sur l’énergie  (EIA) publiée le 24 août 2026. Ainsi, cette progression suit la fermeture quasi totale du  détroit d’Ormuz  depuis fin février, qui a privé l’ Afrique  et l’ Europe  d’une partie des carburants venus du  Golfe . En effet, les expéditions nigérianes ont d’abord bondi à l’ouverture de l’usine en 2024, puis une seconde fois en 2026,  « coïncidant avec les contraintes d’approvisionnement venues d’Ormuz » , écrit l’EIA.
Une capacité relevée juste avant la guerre
Dans un premier temps, la capacité de traitement est passée de 650 000 à 700 000 barils par jour en février, à l’issue d’une phase de maintenance. Ensuite, le régulateur nigérian a relevé un taux d’utilisation de 105,21 % en août, soit 736 470 barils de brut traités chaque jour. Enfin, le groupe y voit  « la contribution croissante de la raffinerie à la sécurité énergétique du Nigeria » , a affirmé le groupe Dangote.
Par conséquent, le pays, qui importait près de 400 000 barils par jour de produits raffinés avant l’ouverture de l’usine, en reçoit désormais moins de 130 000 par voie maritime, toujours selon l’EIA. En parallèle, les livraisons vers l’Europe ont atteint 130 000 barils par jour au deuxième trimestre.
Premier exportateur mondial de kérosène en avril
Au départ,  David Bird , patron de la raffinerie, disait en mars ne pas constater de forte hausse des commandes liée au conflit, alors que les prix réagissaient déjà. Puis l’usine a basculé dans un  « mode de production maximale de carburant d’aviation » , a déclaré David Bird, et elle est devenue en avril le premier exportateur mondial de ce produit. De même, le groupe a accru ses ventes d’urée, un engrais dont près d’un cinquième des exportations mondiales passait par Ormuz avant la guerre, a indiqué  Aliko Dangote  début avril.
Désormais, les comptes suivent : le groupe affiche un bénéfice net de 4,73 milliards de dollars sur les neuf premiers mois de 2026, selon les chiffres publiés à l’approche de son introduction en Bourse, dont les documents ont été signés le 7 septembre. Pourtant, ce gain reste celui d’une entreprise privée. En effet, l’usine achète une partie de son brut sur les marchés internationaux, alors que le Nigeria n’a pas atteint ses objectifs de production pétrolière cette année.

items.title: Détroit d'Ormuz : l'AIE range l'Afrique parmi les régions les plus touchées

original_payload.original_title: Détroit d'Ormuz : l'AIE range l'Afrique parmi les régions les plus touchées
original_payload.original_body:
Image by Engin Akyurt from Pixabay
Détroit d'Ormuz : l'AIE range l'Afrique parmi les régions les plus touchées
27/11/2026    par    Francis Noude
Facebook  Twitter  WhatsApp
L’ Agence internationale de l’énergie  (AIE) classe l’ Afrique  parmi les régions les plus touchées par le blocage du  détroit d’Ormuz , dans son  rapport annuel  publié le 19 novembre 2026 à  Paris . Ce World Energy Outlook 2026 parle du plus grand choc d’approvisionnement énergétique jamais vécu par le monde. Le passage est quasi fermé depuis fin février, quand la guerre entre les  États-Unis ,  Israël  et l’ Iran  a commencé, et aucun accord n’a encore permis de le rouvrir.
Dans le résumé du rapport, les économies en développement d’Asie-Pacifique et d’Afrique figurent parmi les importateurs les plus affectés. De plus, l’agence écarte l’idée d’une crise passée :  « à ce jour, en novembre, elle n’est pas terminée » , écrit l’AIE. Ensuite, son directeur exécutif,  Fatih Birol , va plus loin dans l’avant-propos :  « la crise d’Ormuz a créé la plus grande menace pour la sécurité énergétique de l’histoire » , écrit-il.
Un continent importateur face à des prix qui restent élevés
La plupart des pays africains achètent à l’étranger l’essence et le gasoil qu’ils consomment. Ainsi, chaque secousse du marché les touche directement. Le baril de Brent s’échangeait autour de 95 dollars le 27 novembre, contre environ 70 dollars avant le début de la guerre. Il est donc redescendu par rapport au printemps, mais il reste nettement au-dessus de son niveau d’avant le conflit.
Pourtant, la sortie de crise dépend d’un bras de fer diplomatique.  Téhéran  propose de rouvrir le détroit en deux jours, mais exige d’abord des engagements américains, dont la levée de sanctions récentes, a indiqué son ministre des Affaires étrangères,  Abbas Araghchi . En parallèle, le  Qatar  et le  Pakistan  poursuivent leur médiation. Par conséquent, plus la crise dure, plus ses effets s’installent, prévient l’AIE.
La Côte d’Ivoire gèle la pompe, l’industrie paie
La  Côte d’Ivoire  montre comment un État peut amortir le choc. Une note du gouvernement ivoirien maintient du 1er au 30 novembre le litre de super à 905 FCFA et celui de gasoil à 725 FCFA, soit les mêmes tarifs depuis trois mois. En effet, il y a un an, l’essence se vendait 820 FCFA le litre à  Abidjan , soit 10 % de moins.
Les autorités présentent ce gel comme une protection du pouvoir d’achat des ménages. Mais le coût se déplace vers d’autres acteurs : le butane vrac destiné aux industriels a bondi de 36 %, et le prix du maintien à la pompe n’est pas publié. Enfin, une réunion de l’ OPEP+  est prévue le 29 novembre et pourrait peser sur les cours des prochaines semaines.

items.title: GTA 6 : les bugs du lancement sont-ils comparables à Cyberpunk 2077 ?

original_payload.original_title: GTA 6 : les bugs du lancement sont-ils comparables à Cyberpunk 2077 ?
original_payload.original_body:
Photo Rockstar
GTA 6 : les bugs du lancement sont-ils comparables à Cyberpunk 2077 ?
27/11/2026    par    Hervé Ahanto
Facebook  Twitter  WhatsApp
Des clips de bugs de  GTA 6  circulent sur X et YouTube depuis la sortie du jeu, le 19 novembre 2026. Le site spécialisé   PC Guide   les a recensés. Il conclut que le titre du studio américain  Rockstar Games  reste loin du fiasco de  Cyberpunk 2077 , lancé en décembre 2020. Pourtant, la comparaison s’est imposée sur les réseaux, ce qui pose une question simple : ce lancement ressemble-t-il vraiment à celui de 2020 ?
Des personnages qui traversent le décor
Le streamer  Michael Does Life  a publié une scène où deux personnages se superposent et traversent du mobilier pendant une altercation avec un policier. Ensuite, son confrère  JasonTheWeen  a montré un grand bateau qui bouge de façon étrange près d’un pont. D’autres clips montrent  Lucia , l’une des deux protagonistes, tomber à travers le sol pendant une mission, ou un joueur sortir de la carte. Enfin, des vidéos de véhicules propulsés dans les airs après une collision circulent aussi sur X.
Les critiques ont relevé des défauts du même ordre. Ainsi, «  des petits bugs, comme des piétons qui marchent dans les murs et restent coincés  », a écrit le critique du  Sydney Morning Herald  dans son test. Cependant, «  loin d’être aussi cassé que Cyberpunk 2077  », juge PC Guide à propos de l’ensemble du jeu. Selon le site, les premiers signalements ne semblent pas toucher la majorité des joueurs, et les critiques sont très positives. En revanche, il mentionne des inquiétudes sur les performances, surtout sur la  PS5  de base, sans les relier à un bug précis.
Pourquoi la comparaison a des limites
Cyberpunk 2077 avait connu des problèmes techniques généralisés à sa sortie, surtout sur les anciennes consoles. Ainsi,  Sony  avait retiré temporairement le jeu du  PlayStation Store  et proposé des remboursements complets. Par contraste, GTA 6 n’est pas sorti sur PS4 ni sur Xbox One, ce que PC Guide présente comme une raison de cette différence. Pour le site, les plantages représentent donc le principal risque pour Rockstar, et il s’attend à des correctifs.
Le studio a déjà diffusé deux mises à jour avant le lancement, le 13 puis le 16 novembre, de 1,07 Go et de 602 Mo sur PS5. Cependant, aucune note détaillée ne les accompagnait. De même, les clips recensés ne précisent pas sur quelle console ils ont été enregistrés, ce qui empêche pour l’instant de savoir si un modèle de console est plus touché qu’un autre.
