items.title: 2027: OK Movement withdraws support for Obi, NDC

original_payload.original_title: 2027: OK Movement withdraws support for Obi, NDC
original_payload.original_body:
Politics  2027: OK Movement withdraws support for Obi, NDC
By  Nefisetu Yakubu   ·   8 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Naomi Sharang
The Obidient/Kwankwaso (OK) Movement has announced the withdrawal of its political structures, campaign and mobilisation support for Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), following a breakdown in its political relationship with the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi.
National ​‌‌​​‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​‍⁠‍​‌‌‌​Director-General of the movement, Mr John Ughulu, announced this in a statement on Friday in Abuja.
Ughulu said the movement had been formally informed that Obi and NDC had decided to discontinue their political relationship with the organisation.
While describing the development as regrettable, he, however, said that the movement respected the decision and appreciated Obi for the engagements and opportunities shared with it.
Consequently, he said the movement had resolved to discontinue all campaign, mobilisation and operational support for the party with immediate effect.
He added that all the movement’s political structures at the ward, local government and state levels had been withdrawn from the party’s campaign and mobilisation activities.
The national director-general said the movement recognised NDC’s considerable social media following but noted that such support needed to translate into grassroots political participation.
“The responsibility for converting that support into electoral strength now rests with the party and its leadership,” he said.
Ughulu said the movement would announce its preferred political party and presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections in due course.
He disclosed that the organisation had commenced engagements with other political parties and potential presidential candidates whose political visions and leadership capacity alligned with its principles.
According to him, the movement remains confident in its organisational strength, grassroots presence and mobilisation capacity across the country.
He said the movement’s political direction would be guided by its commitment to integrity, fairness, equity, justice, competence, accountability and national unity.
Ughulu stated that the organisation would not allow personal interests or individual political ambitions to determine its decisions.
He also acknowledged the fact that some members might feel disappointed by the development, having developed political and emotional attachments to NDC.
Ughulu said members were free to maintain their relationship with the party or pursue other political directions without intimidation or hostility.
“We must distinguish between individual political choices and the collective institutional decisions of the OK Movement,” he said.
He urged members, coordinators and volunteers to remain calm, disciplined and focused, while awaiting further directives from the national leadership.
Ughulu reaffirmed the movement’s independence, saying no individual, political party or political interest owned it.
“The OK Movement is not retreating. We are repositioning, reorganising and preparing for the next phase of our political journey,” he said.
He appreciated members and supporters for their sacrifices, resilience and commitment, assuring them that their contributions to building the organisation had not been in vain.
In his reaction, the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Mr Osa Director, described the movement’s withdrawal of support for Obi and NDC as mere political delusion.
“So many rogue elements are parading themselves as OK Movement, and they are entitled to their political delusions.
“We know that the genuine and authentic OK Movement and its leadership is solidly behind the Obi/Kwankwaso ticket.
“Obi and NDC will win the presidential election with the massive support and show of love by Nigerians,” Director said.
(NAN)

items.title: 2027: INEC vows to surpass Osun election success

original_payload.original_title: 2027: INEC vows to surpass Osun election success
original_payload.original_body:
Politics  2027: INEC vows to surpass Osun election success
By  Nefisetu Yakubu   ·   7 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Emmanuel Oloniruha
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it is determined to surpass the successes recorded in recent off-cycle elections in conducting the 2027 general elections.
INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the Gbong Gwom Jos, Da Jacob Buba, at his palace in Jos.
Amupitan expressed the commission’s commitment to conducting credible elections that would strengthen national unity and deepen public confidence in Nigeria’s electoral process.
He said all elections conducted since his assumption of office in October 2025 had been conclusive and successful, without post-election violence.
Amupitan identified the Anambra, Ekiti and Osun governorship elections, alongside the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council elections, as evidence of progressive improvements.
He described the Osun governorship election as particularly successful, citing its impressive voter turnout.
“So our prayer, our plan, our determination and desire is that the general elections will be more successful than the Osun governorship election.
“It will be an election that will further unite Nigeria and all of us,” he said.
Amupitan also announced that INEC would conduct nationwide mock accreditation on Saturday across 17,656 polling units, comprising two polling units per ward.
He said the exercise would test the efficiency of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and simultaneous transmission of results to the INEC Result Viewing portal.
According to him, the exercise is aimed at preventing a recurrence of the technical glitches experienced during the 2023 presidential election.
Amupitan appealed to traditional rulers to mobilise eligible voters to participate actively in the mock accreditation and the general elections.
He also sought their support in combating misinformation and disinformation ahead of the elections.
The chairman warned that malicious actors could deploy Artificial Intelligence (AI) and deepfake videos to mislead citizens and suppress voter turnout.
He urged Nigerians to verify information circulating on social media before acting on it.
“We want our people to come out and vote in this election. Your voice is very weighty, not just in Jos, not just in Plateau, but all over the country,” he said.
Amupitan described his visit as a homecoming, saying it was also to formally notify the traditional ruler of the election dates and seek his support.
Responding, Buba, Chairman of the Plateau State Council of Chiefs and Emirs, expressed confidence in Amupitan’s integrity and capacity to deliver credible elections.
The traditional ruler urged the INEC chairman to remain steadfast in discharging his responsibilities, irrespective of political pressure, criticism and threats.
“Even with the noise, the attacks, as long as you convince yourself you’re doing the right thing, you will always have the strength to move ahead,” he said.
Buba reaffirmed the commitment of traditional rulers to mobilising eligible citizens to register and participate in elections.
He assured INEC of the council’s continued support and prayed for divine wisdom and strength for Amupitan to discharge his responsibilities effectively. (NAN)

items.title: MTN graduates 5th media innovation cohort, pledges sustainability

original_payload.original_title: MTN graduates 5th media innovation cohort, pledges sustainability
original_payload.original_body:
General News  MTN graduates 5th media innovation cohort, pledges sustainability
By  Nefisetu Yakubu   ·   58 minutes ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Usman Aliyu
MTN Nigeria has pledged to sustain its Media Innovation Programme (MIP), saying continuous investment in journalists is critical to strengthening media independence, public trust and democratic accountability.
Mr Tobe Okigbo, Chief Corporate Services and Sustainability Officer of MTN Nigeria, gave the assurance on Friday in Lagos at the graduation of the programme’s fifth cohort.
Okigbo was represented by Mr Funsho Aina, Senior Manager, External Relations at MTN Nigeria.
The MTN chief  said the initiative, introduced in 2022 as a three-year pilot in partnership with the School of Media and Communication, Pan-Atlantic University, had evolved into a flagship intervention for strengthening journalism in Nigeria.
He said that no fewer than 100 journalists and content creators had benefited from the programme, which was initially conceived as a pilot but attracted growing demand and international recognition.
“When we started, we just thought, let’s start with a pilot and see how it goes. But in a year or two, it became so popular and highly demanded that it even won international awards,” he said.
Okigbo said the company had no intention of discontinuing the initiative, given the continuing need to strengthen professional capacity in the media industry.
“With your continuous support, I can promise you that we will continue with the Media Innovation Programme. It is not going to stop,” he said.
He explained that MTN’s intervention was informed by the important role of the media in holding institutions accountable and providing accurate information to society.
According to him, the media is a public trust, but several challenges, including irregular payment of salaries and inadequate investment in professional development, continue to undermine the industry.
He said the rapid emergence of new technologies and changing media practices had made continuous training increasingly necessary for journalists and content creators.
“We believe that the best thing we can do for the media is to help the media build capacity. And not just any ordinary capacity, real capacity,” he said.
Okigbo said MTN partnered with Pan-Atlantic University to ensure that the programme delivered structured and credible professional training.
He added that building a viable and credible media ecosystem was consistent with the company’s broader commitment to nation-building and its responsibilities to stakeholders, including customers, regulators, technology partners and the media.
Okigbo also stressed that corporate support for journalism must not compromise editorial independence.
“MTN supports this programme, but we do not own your newsroom, your byline or your conscience,” he said.
He added that participation in the programme did not oblige beneficiaries to report favourably about the company, insisting that journalists must scrutinise MTN with the same rigour applied to other institutions.
“If MTN does something that deserves scrutiny, I expect you to report it with the same rigour you would bring to anyone else,” he said.
He argued that media independence was closely linked to the financial sustainability of news organisations, noting that newsrooms unable to sustain themselves could become vulnerable to external pressure.
“A newsroom that cannot sustain itself is vulnerable to pressure, and an industry that cannot pay its way struggles to remain fearless,” he said.
He, therefore, described strengthening the business of media as inseparable from protecting its integrity.
Addressing the graduating fellows, Okigbo urged them to share the knowledge acquired during the programme with colleagues who might not have access to similar professional development opportunities.
He drew on a quotation by American poet and civil rights activist Maya Angelou, saying: “I come as one, but I stand as ten thousand.”
He challenged the fellows to become advocates of professional development in their newsrooms and wider media communities.
“We want you to go out not only having imbibed everything that has been taught, but we also want you to help in democratising knowledge.
“Whatever happens, remember that you came as one, please leave as ten thousand,” he said.
He also urged journalists to preserve the core values of accuracy, fairness, courage and depth amid the pressures of misinformation, emerging technologies and changing the audience behaviour.
Okigbo compared the continuity of journalism to the rebuilding of Japan’s Ise Grand Shrine every 20 years, a tradition through which knowledge, discipline and craftsmanship are passed from one generation to another.
He said the profession could endure only when experienced journalists deliberately transferred its standards and values to those coming behind them. (NAN)
AUO/VIV
=====

items.title: 2027: SDP candidate promises N200 petrol, free healthcare

original_payload.original_title: 2027: SDP candidate promises N200 petrol, free healthcare
original_payload.original_body:
Politics  2027: SDP candidate promises N200 petrol, free healthcare
By  Funmilayo Adeyemi   ·   1 hour ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Awayi Kuje
The presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Dr Adewole Adebayo, has promised to reduce petrol prices to N200 per litre without subsidy and provide free healthcare if elected president in 2027.
He also pledged free and compulsory education, increased food production, job creation and improved welfare for persons living with disabilities.
Adebayo made the promises at an SDP town hall meeting with party leaders, candidates and supporters in Nasarawa State.
He urged Nigerians to use the 2027 general election to determine the country’s leadership through the ballot, stressing the importance of electoral participation.
Adebayo said the SDP had developed policy proposals to address poverty, unemployment, high living costs and other economic challenges facing the country.
On fuel pricing, he said an SDP-led government would reduce petrol prices to N200 per litre without subsidy through improved efficiency and measures to address corruption in the petroleum sector.
“We will give you petrol for N200 per litre without subsidy. We will sell it for N200, and NNPC will still make a profit because we will stop funding corruption,” he said.
On agriculture, Adebayo said Nasarawa and neighbouring states had the potential to contribute significantly to national food production.
“Nasarawa alone can feed Nigeria. Nasarawa, Plateau, Kogi, Kaduna and the Federal Capital Territory have the capacity to feed the whole of Africa,” he said.
He also promised free and compulsory education, including measures to expand access to schooling for out-of-school children.
According to him, an SDP administration would integrate children in the Almajiri system into formal education while ensuring they continued to receive religious instruction.
On healthcare, Adebayo proposed establishing a Federal Medical Centre in every federal constituency and introducing compulsory medical check-ups four times annually.
He also promised free medical consultations and medication, although he did not provide details of the proposed funding arrangements.
On employment, the SDP candidate pledged to create more job opportunities, including for persons living with disabilities.
He also promised to develop Nasarawa’s mineral resources, including gold, coal, lithium and copper, to promote economic growth and improve the welfare of host communities.
Adebayo endorsed the SDP governorship candidate in the state, former Inspector-General of Police, Abubakar Adamu, saying his experience in policing would be an asset in addressing security challenges.
He urged voters to assess political candidates based on their records, character and policy proposals rather than party affiliations.
The presidential candidate also called for an enabling environment for opposition parties to participate in the electoral process, stressing the importance of political competition in a democracy.
Earlier, the SDP National Chairman, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, urged Nasarawa residents to support Adebayo, Adamu and other party candidates in the 2027 elections.
Gombe said the town hall meeting provided an opportunity for the party to engage residents, hear their concerns and present its programmes.
He urged party members to remain united and participate peacefully in the electoral process.
Also speaking, Adamu said the meeting provided an opportunity to interact with residents and understand their expectations of the next state administration.
He identified security, justice, accountability and citizens’ welfare as priorities, pledging to incorporate public concerns into government decisions.
The meeting was attended by SDP national and state leaders, National Assembly and State House of Assembly candidates, as well as party supporters. (NAN)

The Executive Secretary of the Lateef Jakande Leadership Academy (LJLA), Mrs Ayisat Agbaje-Okunade, has won the 2026 Exemplary Leadership Award.

items.title: Zamfara bars public schools from mobilising students to welcome politicians

original_payload.original_title: Zamfara bars public schools from mobilising students to welcome politicians
original_payload.original_body:
THE Zamfara State Government has banned the mobilisation of public school pupils and students to line up along roadsides to welcome political office holders, political leaders and other dignitaries during electioneering campaigns.
The state Commissioner for Education, Science and Technology, Malam Abdulmalik Abubakar Gajam gave the order on Friday, November 27, according to a statement issued by the ministry’s Information and Public Relations Officer, Bashir Abashiya.
The policy was introduced to protect classroom hours and prevent learners from being drawn into political activities, said the commissioner.
“The directive is aimed at ensuring that schools remain focused on their primary responsibility of providing quality education and that students and pupils are not unnecessarily taken away from their academic activities or exposed to political campaign activities,” the statement read.
Gajam instructed education secretaries, zonal education officers, principals, and headteachers across Zamfara State to enforce the order within their respective jurisdictions. He warned that school officials must not instruct, encourage, or compel any learner to leave school premises or assemble along roadsides for political receptions.

items.title: Élimination du Cancer du col de l’utérus : Le Bénin accélère la mobilisation pour sauver des vies

original_payload.original_title: Élimination du Cancer du col de l’utérus : Le Bénin accélère la mobilisation pour sauver des vies
original_payload.original_body:
La prévention, la vaccination, le dépistage et la prise en charge précoces constituent les principaux leviers de la riposte contre le cancer du col de l’utérus. Ces priorités ont été au cœur de la célébration de la Journée mondiale consacrée à l’élimination de cette maladie, ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026 à Cotonou.
Autour du thème : « Ensemble, éliminons le cancer du col de l’utérus : protéger les filles aujourd’hui, sauver les femmes demain », la cérémonie a réuni plusieurs personnalités, notamment les Ministres Sèdami MDEGAN FAGLA, de l'enseignement supérieur et de la recherche scientifique, chargée de la Formation technique, et Adéyèmi Clément KOUCHADE, de l’Enseignement secondaire, des têtes couronnées, des acteurs du système sanitaire béninois et de la sous-région, ainsi que des partenaires techniques et financiers.
À l’ouverture des travaux, le Préfet du Littoral, Monsieur Gilbert DEOU MALE, a lancé un appel à une mobilisation collective et urgente face à cette maladie. « La lutte contre le cancer du col de l’utérus doit être une véritable cause nationale qui rassemble tous les acteurs de la société », a-t-il souligné.
Représentant les partenaires techniques et financiers, le Représentant résident de l’UNICEF au Bénin, Monsieur Ousmane NIANG, a salué les efforts du Gouvernement et rappelé le caractère évitable de cette maladie. « Le cancer du col de l’utérus est une maladie évitable et nous disposons des moyens pour l’éliminer et l’éradiquer », a-t-il affirmé, réitérant l’engagement des partenaires à soutenir les politiques nationales, la mobilisation communautaire et le renforcement des capacités des agents de santé.
Pour sa part, la Directrice exécutive de Women in Global Health, Dr Magda ROBALO, a adressé un appel en cinq points aux gouvernants : investir dans les programmes nationaux, renforcer le dépistage des femmes vulnérables, soutenir les personnels soignants, partager le pouvoir et mettre fin aux violences faites aux femmes et aux filles.
Dans son intervention, le ministre de la Santé, le Professeur Benjamin HOUNKPATIN, a rappelé l'adhésion du Bénin à la stratégie mondiale de l’OMS, qui vise à vacciner 90 % des filles contre le HPV avant 15 ans, dépister 70 % des femmes à 35 et 45 ans et prendre en charge 90 % des femmes présentant des lésions ou un cancer du col d’ici 2030.
Inscrite dans le Plan national de développement sanitaire 2026-2030 et le Plan national de lutte contre les cancers 2024-2028, cette ambition se traduit par des actions concrètes. « Le vaccin est intégré au Programme élargi de vaccination : il est disponible dans tous les centres de santé publics du Bénin, gratuit et administré au quotidien aux filles de neuf ans », a rassuré le Ministre. Il a enfin rappelé trois gestes essentiels : vacciner les filles de neuf ans et rattraper celles de 10 à 14 ans non encore vaccinées, dépister les femmes dès 25 ans selon les recommandations sanitaires et traiter précocement toutes les lésions précancéreuses.
La mobilisation des autorités, des professionnels de santé, des partenaires et des communautés demeure déterminante pour faire reculer cette maladie et renforcer la protection des filles et des femmes.

original_payload.original_title: Bénin : 16 victimes recensées dans un accident de bus à Sirarou
original_payload.original_body:
Un accident de bus à Sirarou a fait 16 victimes dans la nuit du vendredi 27 novembre 2026, à la sortie de Parakou. Les secours ont évacué neuf blessés au CHD du Borgou et sept autres à l’hôpital de Boko. Aucun décès n’a été signalé dans le bilan provisoire.
Un grave accident de la circulation a impliqué un bus immatriculé en Côte d’Ivoire, dans la nuit du vendredi 27 novembre 2026. Le drame s’est produit vers 21h16, au village de Mareborou, avant le poste de péage de Sirarou. Situé à la sortie de Parakou, dans le département du Borgou, le lieu de l’accident a rapidement accueilli les équipes de secours. Le bilan provisoire fait état de 16 victimes, sans perte en vie humaine.
Accident de bus à Sirarou : les secours évacuent 16 victimes
Alertés après l’accident, les éléments de l’Agence béninoise de protection civile (ABPC) du Borgou se sont rendus sur les lieux. Le capitaine-major Fayomi, chef de l’Antenne départementale, a conduit l’intervention. Les équipes ont organisé les premiers secours et procédé à l’évacuation des victimes vers les structures sanitaires.
Selon les informations communiquées par l’ABPC, neuf victimes ont rejoint le Centre hospitalier départemental (CHD) du Borgou. Les secours ont également transporté sept autres personnes à l’hôpital de Boko. Des citoyens présents sur les lieux ont apporté leur concours à cette seconde évacuation.
Au total, les services de secours ont recensé 16 victimes. Aucun décès n’a été signalé dans le bilan provisoire communiqué après l’intervention. Les autorités sanitaires et les services compétents poursuivent la prise en charge des personnes concernées.
Les circonstances de l’accident restent à déterminer
Pour l’heure, les causes de cet accident de bus à Sirarou demeurent inconnues. Les circonstances dans lesquelles le véhicule a quitté ou perdu le contrôle de sa trajectoire restent à établir. Des investigations policières devraient permettre de mieux comprendre le déroulement des faits.
L’immatriculation ivoirienne du bus constitue également un élément d’identification du véhicule impliqué. Les résultats des investigations permettront de préciser les responsabilités éventuelles et les facteurs ayant provoqué cet accident.
L’ABPC appelle les conducteurs à la vigilance avant les fêtes
Cet accident survient à quelques semaines des fêtes de fin d’année. Cette période entraîne généralement une augmentation des déplacements sur les routes béninoises. Les risques d’accidents deviennent alors une préoccupation majeure pour les autorités chargées de la sécurité routière.
Face à cette situation, l’Agence béninoise de protection civile invite les usagers à renforcer leur vigilance. Son appel concerne particulièrement les conducteurs de véhicules particuliers et les professionnels du transport.
L’agence recommande d’abord le respect strict des limitations de vitesse. Elle insiste également sur la prudence pendant les dépassements. Les conducteurs doivent aussi éviter de prendre le volant sous l’emprise de l’alcool.
Par ailleurs, l’ABPC conseille aux automobilistes de bien se reposer avant chaque déplacement. Elle leur demande également de vérifier l’état mécanique de leurs véhicules avant de prendre la route.
Ces mesures visent à prévenir les accidents et à protéger les usagers pendant les déplacements de fin d’année. À Sirarou, les circonstances exactes du drame restent attendues, tandis que le bilan provisoire ne fait état d’aucun décès.

items.title: Bénin : 8 projets pour réduire les coupures d’électricité

original_payload.original_title: Bénin : 8 projets pour réduire les coupures d’électricité
original_payload.original_body:
Finir avec les coupures d’électricité qui continuent de perturber les activités économiques et le quotidien des populations au Bénin. C’est l’objectif visé par le gouvernement. Il s’agit de produire davantage d’électricité sur le territoire national. Car le pays veut aussi réduire sa dépendance aux importations, notamment en provenance du Nigeria et du Ghana. Pour y parvenir, il mise sur le développement de nouvelles infrastructures de production électrique. Au total, six projets solaires, le barrage hydroélectrique de Dogo-Bis et une centrale thermique à Glo-Djigbé figurent parmi les investissements annoncés. Ces installations doivent accroître la capacité nationale de production, diversifier les sources d’énergie et réduire la dépendance du Bénin aux importations d’électricité.
6 projets solaires pour diversifier la production électrique
Le premier volet porte sur le développement de l’énergie solaire. À ce niveau, 6 projets sont prévus dans plusieurs localités du pays. Il s’agit de 4 centrales photovoltaïques à Natitingou, Djougou, Parakou et Bohicon. À ces infrastructures s’ajoutent l’extension de la centrale solaire d’Illoulofin, à Pobè, et une nouvelle installation à Kandi.
Les 4 centrales photovoltaïques afficheront une capacité cumulée de 50 MW en courant alternatif. Dans le détail, Natitingou et Djougou accueilleront chacune une centrale de 10 MW. Parakou et Bohicon disposeront, quant à elles, d’installations de 15 MW chacune. Leur construction permettra d’injecter davantage d’électricité dans le réseau national. Elle contribuera également à rapprocher les capacités de production des villes du nord et du centre du pays. Pour financer ces infrastructures, le gouvernement mobilise des ressources auprès de partenaires internationaux et du secteur privé. Selon la Société financière internationale (IFC), le projet pourrait fournir de l’électricité à environ 383 000 personnes.
À Pobè, le gouvernement prévoit de faire passer la centrale solaire d’Illoulofin de 25 à 75 MW. Cette extension doit tripler sa capacité initiale. Elle permettra donc d’accroître la quantité d’électricité solaire disponible sur le réseau. À Kandi, un autre projet solaire doit renforcer la production dans le nord du pays. La Société béninoise de production d’électricité (SBPE) répertorie actuellement une installation de 10 MW en cours.
Ces projets solaires utilisent une ressource renouvelable et réduisent la consommation de combustibles fossiles. Leur production dépend néanmoins de l’ensoleillement. Le stockage et la complémentarité avec d’autres centrales restent donc essentiels pour assurer une alimentation régulière, notamment la nuit.
Le barrage hydroélectrique de Dogo-Bis va produire 128 MW
Le deuxième grand projet concerne le barrage hydroélectrique multifonctionnel de Dogo-Bis. Prévu dans la vallée de l’Ouémé, cet ouvrage doit développer la production nationale d’électricité à partir de l’eau. Sa future centrale disposera d’une puissance installée de 128 MW. Le projet prévoit également 30 MWc de solaire flottant, selon le Pacte national de l’énergie du Bénin.
Contrairement aux centrales solaires, une centrale hydroélectrique utilise la force de l’eau pour faire tourner des turbines. Ces turbines entraînent des générateurs qui produisent de l’électricité. Dogo-Bis doit donc apporter une source complémentaire aux installations solaires et thermiques. Le gouvernement espère également réduire les coûts de production grâce à cette énergie renouvelable.
Mais les retombées du barrage ne se limiteront pas à l’électricité. Le projet prévoit aussi l’aménagement de périmètres agricoles irrigués. Il doit contribuer à mieux gérer les ressources en eau et à réduire les risques d’inondation dans la vallée de l’Ouémé. Le financement du projet bénéficie notamment d’un accord de 150 millions de dollars signé avec la Banque mondiale en juillet 2026. Sa mise en service est envisagée pour la période 2027-2028. Ce calendrier reste prévisionnel.
Glo-Djigbé : une centrale thermique de 140 MW
Le troisième volet repose sur la construction d’une centrale thermique à cycle combiné à Glo-Djigbé, dans la commune d’Abomey-Calavi. Cette infrastructure doit disposer d’une puissance de 140 MW. Elle fonctionnera avec deux types de combustibles, selon le principe du système dual fuel.
Son principal avantage réside dans sa capacité à produire de l’électricité indépendamment de l’ensoleillement. Elle pourra donc compléter les centrales solaires lorsque leur production baisse. La SBPE présente ce projet comme étant en cours de développement. Le coût estimatif affiché par le programme d’action du gouvernement atteint 130 milliards de FCFA.
Cette centrale doit renforcer la disponibilité de l’électricité et apporter une capacité supplémentaire au réseau national. Son fonctionnement dépendra néanmoins de la disponibilité et du coût des combustibles nécessaires à sa production.
87,288 milliards de FCFA pour le programme Énergie
Ces 8 infrastructures traduisent une volonté d’augmenter les capacités nationales de production. Leur réalisation pourrait réduire la pression sur les importations et améliorer la sécurité énergétique du pays.
Le projet de budget 2027 prévoit 87,288 milliards de FCFA pour le programme Énergie. Cette enveloppe comprend notamment 86,985 milliards de crédits de paiement consacrés aux dépenses en capital. Le document budgétaire ne détaille toutefois pas la répartition de ces crédits entre les huit infrastructures.
Un autre défi demeure : le transport et la distribution de l’électricité. Même lorsque les centrales produisent suffisamment, des lignes surchargées ou des postes défaillants peuvent provoquer des interruptions. Le gouvernement doit donc poursuivre la modernisation du réseau et renforcer les postes de transformation. Il devra également améliorer le stockage et la gestion de la demande.

items.title: NEC sets 50 million SSP fee for presidential hopefuls

original_payload.original_title: NEC sets 50 million SSP fee for presidential hopefuls
original_payload.original_body:
South Sudan’s National Elections Commission (NEC) has set a nomination deposit of 50 million South Sudanese pounds for presidential candidates contesting the February 11, 2027, general elections.
In a notice issued by the commission in Juba on Saturday, nominations will open on November 29, 2026, and close on January 21, 2027, covering the presidency, governorships, administrative area chief administrators and seats in national and state legislative assemblies.
The announcement comes as voter registration is due to close today evening after a two-week exercise across the country.
The commission has also set a deposit of 30 million pounds for candidates seeking governorships and the positions of chief administrators of the three administrative areas.
Candidates contesting geographical constituencies in the National Legislative Assembly, as well as those on national women’s and political party lists, will pay 20 million pounds.
For state legislative assemblies, candidates contesting geographical constituencies, women’s lists and political party lists will pay 15 million pounds. Political party lists for administrative area legislative councils carry a deposit of 10 million pounds.
The notice specifies one seat for the presidency, 10 governorships and three administrative area chief administrators. It also lists 102 geographical constituency seats, 71 women’s list seats and 31 political party list seats in the National Legislative Assembly.
At state level, the notice allocates 29 geographical constituency seats, 20 women’s list seats and nine political party list seats in each state legislative assembly. Administrative area legislative councils have 20 seats for political party lists in each area.
The commission said nomination forms are available on its website and at NEC offices. Applicants must submit completed application forms, supporting documents and proof of payment into the commission’s bank account.
Presidential candidates must submit their applications at NEC headquarters in Juba, while gubernatorial nominations will be received by the respective State High Election Committees. Applications for administrative area chief administrators will be submitted to the relevant Administrative Area High Election Committees.
For National Legislative Assembly geographical constituencies, nominations will be received by the relevant State High Election Committee or Administrative Area High Election Committee, depending on the constituency. Applications for national women’s and political party lists must be submitted at NEC headquarters in Juba.
State legislative assembly nominations will be submitted to the respective State High Election Committees, while political party lists for administrative area legislative councils will be received by the relevant Administrative Area High Election Committees.
The notice says candidates, their nominating political parties or authorised representatives may submit applications for presidential, gubernatorial, chief administrator and geographical constituency positions. Applications for women’s and party lists must be submitted by persons authorised by the respective political parties.
The electoral body says its offices will receive applications daily from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The commission said it would publish the list of applicants by January 28, with complaints against the list allowed within seven days of publication. No fee will be charged for complaints or appeals.
The notice also states that members of state legislative assemblies and administrative area legislative councils will elect the Council of States after the respective bodies convene. Nominations for those positions will be announced separately.
South Sudan is scheduled to hold general elections on February 11, 2027, following a revision of the electoral timetable.

items.title: Opinion| Kings at the Ballot Box: Should South Sudan’s traditional rulers vote?

original_payload.original_title: Opinion| Kings at the Ballot Box: Should South Sudan’s traditional rulers vote?
original_payload.original_body:
Community kings in South Sudan, among them the Reth of the Shilluk Kingdom and the king of the Azande Kingdom, are traditional rulers, not heads of state. I know of no national law that stops them from voting on the same basis as other eligible citizens. Yet tradition expects them to stay above party politics. As the country moves toward elections, that tension deserves a closer look.
A symbol of unity
A community king belongs to everyone in his kingdom, whatever their party or political camp. He is expected to stand above partisan competition, and a publicly declared party preference could divide his people and weaken the trust they place in him.
Guardians of custom and order
Kings are custodians of culture, custom and social order. The Shilluk Reth guides ritual life and approves village chiefs. The Azande king is responsible for the social order and security of his kingdom. Staying outside partisan politics allows a king to work with whichever government, party or leader holds power in the state or nation.
Authority rooted in tradition
The anthropologist Evans-Pritchard famously described the Shilluk Reth as a ruler who “reigned but did not rule”. His authority comes from custom, not from secular political power. Today South Sudan’s kings are traditional authorities within the state, not independent political leaders, and that standing depends on remaining above political competition.
The Azande example
The Azande Kingdom is based in Yambio, in Western Equatoria. Its best-known ruler, King Gbudwe, ruled from 1870 to 1905 and was killed after resisting British forces. The monarchy was restored on 9 February 2022, when his great-grandson, Atoroba Peni Rikito Gbudue, was crowned after 117 years without a king.
This week, King Atoroba was reported to have registered to vote at a centre in Yambio. He urged eligible citizens to register and to choose their leaders peacefully.
Participation without partisanship
The king’s registration shows that taking part in the civic process and staying neutral in party competition are not contradictory. A vote is secret, and registering is an act of citizenship. By setting an example, a respected traditional leader can encourage participation in his community and promote peaceful choices.
The challenge for South Sudan’s kings is to use their moral authority to strengthen democratic participation without becoming advocates for any party. If they manage that, tradition and the ballot box can reinforce each other.
The writer, Boboya James Edmond, is a policy and political analyst; a contributor on good governance and liberal democracy in South Sudan and Africa. He can be reached via  boboyaj40@gmail.com .

items.title: Long distances, delays hamper voter registration in Malakal

original_payload.original_title: Long distances, delays hamper voter registration in Malakal
original_payload.original_body:
Residents in Malakal, Upper Nile State, have raised concerns over long distances to registration centres, delays in issuing voter cards and overcrowding as turnout increased towards the registration deadline.
Dominica Fatok, who registered at one of the centres, told Radio Tamazuj on Thursday that a lack of proper facilities for laminating registration cards was delaying their issuance.
She also called for better access to registration centres for people travelling from remote areas.
Another resident, Julia Obaj, said the distance between the displacement camp in Malakal and registration centres in town is making it difficult for some residents to participate.
She added that increased turnout towards the deadline had contributed to overcrowding.
Peter Mayom, head of the Upper Nile State High Election Committee, said registration was progressing despite operational and logistical challenges.
Speaking to Radio Tamazuj at the State Election Commission headquarters, Mayom said some problems had been resolved.
He cited a lack of electricity to operate card-laminating machines at some centres and delays in releasing operational funds as major obstacles.
“Some centres are experiencing difficulties laminating the registration cards because they do not have electricity to operate the machines,” Mayom said.
He also cited attempts by underage children and foreign nationals to register as voters, as well as increased turnout towards the deadline, as challenges facing the exercise.
Mayom said the National Election Commission’s Deputy Chairman, Dr Francis Luigi Adwok, had visited Upper Nile earlier in the week to assess registration progress and inspect difficulties at various centres.
According to Mayom, Adwok visited several registration sites, witnessed some of the challenges.
Voter registration is scheduled to close on Saturday, November 28. However, registration centres in Wau town remained congested on Saturday morning, with hundreds of people waiting to register.
South Sudan’s general elections are scheduled for February 11, 2027, under the revised timetable announced by the National Elections Commission.

items.title: Elections alone cannot secure lasting peace in South Sudan, UN says

original_payload.original_title: Elections alone cannot secure lasting peace in South Sudan, UN says
original_payload.original_body:
South Sudan’s elections must be a milestone in the peace process, not its conclusion, the head of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) said on Friday, urging continued implementation of outstanding commitments under the 2018 peace agreement.
Anita Kiki Gbeho, the UN secretary-general’s special representative for South Sudan, said elections alone would not guarantee lasting stability, which also depends on respect for the ceasefire, inclusive governance and political reforms.
“Elections are an important milestone, but not an end to the peace process,” Gbeho said at the launch of an African Union-Intergovernmental Authority on Development-United Nations (AU-IGAD-UN) Joint Task Force in Addis Ababa.
Her remarks came a day after President Salva Kiir  closed an inter-party dialogue  in Juba, where participating political parties adopted resolutions on political freedoms, security guarantees and preparations for elections scheduled for February 11, 2027.
The polls, South Sudan’s first since independence in 2011, were initially scheduled for December 22, 2026, but were postponed by the National Elections Commission to allow more time for preparations.
Gbeho said outstanding commitments under the Revitalised Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in South Sudan (R-ARCSS) included a permanent constitution, transitional security arrangements, judicial reform, transitional justice and national reconciliation.
She said the United Nations is ready to support the process through political engagement, good offices, joint assessments and preventive diplomacy, in partnership with the African Union and IGAD.
National ownership
Speaking at the same event on behalf of Kiir, Foreign Minister Cecilia Adut Manyok said the primary responsibility for peace, security, reconciliation and democratic governance rests with South Sudan’s government and people.
“South Sudan acknowledges that the primary responsibility for peace, security, reconciliation and democratic governance rests with its government and its people,” Adut said.
She cited the inter-party dialogue’s resolutions on political freedoms, security guarantees for candidates and their supporters, political party funding and the 35% affirmative action provision for women.
Adut urged international and regional partners to  respect South Sudan’s sovereignty  while providing financial and technical support to help complete the transitional period.
However, the dialogue involved political parties based in Juba and excluded some opposition groups operating outside the country, limiting the breadth of political participation in the process.
Gbeho said building broad consensus requires meaningful and inclusive engagement among all stakeholders, adding that South Sudanese ownership and leadership are indispensable to lasting peace.
She also welcomed a presidential decree on humanitarian access, saying its implementation would help facilitate assistance to people in need.
The senior UN official said the safety, dignity and voices of South Sudanese people must remain at the centre of efforts to secure lasting peace.

original_payload.original_title: Commémoration de la proclamation de la République : « Ce moment rassemble chacun de nous autour de nos valeurs d’unité, de travail et de progrès », Mahamat Idriss Deby Itno

items.title: Céréales : les stocks mondiaux en hausse, le riz en recul attendu

original_payload.original_title: Céréales : les stocks mondiaux en hausse, le riz en recul attendu
original_payload.original_body:
Les stocks mondiaux de céréales devraient continuer de s’étoffer d’ici à la fin de la campagne 2026-2027. En revanche, la production de riz pourrait enregistrer son premier recul en quatre ans. Dans son dernier rapport, publié jeudi, l’Organisation des Nations unies pour l’alimentation et l’agriculture (FAO) alerte sur la forte diminution des exportations de céréales en mer Noire et sur les répercussions possibles du phénomène climatique El Niño sur plusieurs filières agricoles.
Le commerce mondial des céréales devrait reculer de 3,3 % au cours de la campagne 2026-2027, principalement en raison de la contraction des échanges de blé. Les volumes exportés par les principaux pays fournisseurs devraient diminuer. En revanche, les échanges de maïs devraient progresser durant cette campagne, tandis que ceux de riz devraient reprendre en 2027.
La guerre en Ukraine continue de perturber les flux commerciaux en mer Noire. Les expéditions cumulées de céréales depuis les ports ukrainiens de la région d’Odessa et les ports russes de la mer d’Azov et de la mer Noire sont tombées sous la barre des 500 000 tonnes en septembre dernier, contre 7,8 millions de tonnes un an auparavant.
Lire aussi :  Céréales, sucre, huiles : les prix des produits alimentaires grimpent de 5,8% en un an (FAO)
Du côté de la production, les perspectives restent contrastées. Les récoltes mondiales de blé et de maïs devraient se maintenir au-dessus de leurs moyennes des cinq dernières années. En revanche, la production de riz devrait baisser pour la première fois depuis quatre campagnes, sous l’effet conjugué de la faiblesse des marges des producteurs et de conditions climatiques défavorables liées à El Niño.
Ces tensions sur les coûts de production s’inscrivent dans un contexte plus large d’évolution des marchés agricoles, qui se reflète également dans la facture mondiale des importations alimentaires.
Lire aussi :  Le déficit pluviométrique affecte la production de riz à Doba
Celle-ci devrait augmenter de 1,9 % cette année, pour atteindre 2 267 milliards de dollars, après une hausse de près de 8 % en 2025. Ce ralentissement s’explique notamment par la baisse des prix du café et du cacao, qui compense en partie la hausse de la facture des céréales et des oléagineux.

items.title: Novembre Numérique 2026 : l’Institut français du Tchad et Wenaklabs interrogent l’avenir du numérique

original_payload.original_title: Novembre Numérique 2026 : l’Institut français du Tchad et Wenaklabs interrogent l’avenir du numérique
original_payload.original_body:
Dans le cadre de la clôture de l’édition 2026 de Novembre Numérique, l’Institut français du Tchad et Wenaklabs ont organisé, ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026, un grand débat autour du thème « Quel numérique voulons-nous pour demain ? ». La rencontre, tenue à la Médiathèque éphémère de l’IFT, a réuni des experts, des créateurs, des chercheurs, des citoyens et des acteurs du numérique pour réfléchir aux mutations technologiques et à leurs conséquences sur la société.
Au cœur des échanges figuraient plusieurs enjeux majeurs liés à l’évolution du numérique, notamment l’intelligence artificielle, l’éducation, les médias, la création et l’emploi. Les discussions ont également porté sur les transformations sociales induites par les nouvelles technologies, avec une attention particulière accordée aux réalités et aux perspectives de la société tchadienne.
Les participants ont ainsi abordé les opportunités offertes par les outils numériques, mais aussi les risques qu’ils peuvent représenter, notamment en matière de désinformation. L’intelligence artificielle, en particulier, a occupé une place importante dans les réflexions.
Lire aussi  :  Technologie : Wenaklabs lance la 10ème édition du novembre numérique
Intervenant au cours de cette rencontre, l’expert Roland Konodji Guelngar a évoqué les aspects positifs et négatifs de l’intelligence artificielle. Il a notamment mis en garde contre la propagation des fausses informations rendue plus facile par les capacités de ces nouvelles technologies.
«  Il y a des bons et des mauvais côtés. Je commence par les mauvais côtés. Les mauvais côtés, déjà, tout ce qui est fake news, issu des facilités que l’IA donne pour montrer les fausses informations. Du côté positif, l’IA apporte les opportunités d’apprendre, augmenter sa capacité et ses compétences  », a-t-il déclaré.
Cette rencontre de clôture de Novembre Numérique 2026 a notamment permis de mettre en lumière la nécessité de réfléchir aux usages des technologies, entre opportunités d’innovation, développement des compétences et vigilance face aux dérives.

items.title: Tchad : le rôle de la jeunesse dans la démocratie et la consolidation de la paix au cœur d’une conférence

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : le rôle de la jeunesse dans la démocratie et la consolidation de la paix au cœur d’une conférence
original_payload.original_body:
Le Centre africain de la paix a organisé, ce jeudi 26 novembre 2026, au CEFOD, une conférence publique autour du thème : « La contribution de la jeunesse dans le processus démocratique et la consolidation de la paix au Tchad ».
Cette initiative vise notamment à analyser les enjeux et les défis liés à la participation politique et citoyenne des jeunes au processus démocratique au Tchad. Elle entend également examiner leurs contributions actuelles et potentielles à la prévention des conflits, au dialogue social et à la cohésion nationale.
Les échanges ont également porté sur les obstacles institutionnels, sociaux et structurels qui limitent l’engagement des jeunes dans les mécanismes de gouvernance et de consolidation de la paix. La conférence constitue, par ailleurs, un cadre de dialogue entre les institutions de jeunesse, les universitaires et les organisations de la société civile autour de leurs responsabilités partagées en matière de participation démocratique.
Lire aussi :  Journée internationale de la démocratie : réseaux sociaux, nouveaux espaces du débat démocratique ?
Prenant part aux échanges, le président du Conseil national de la jeunesse du Tchad (CNJT), Abakar Dangaya, a rappelé l’importance de la participation de toutes les composantes de la société au fonctionnement démocratique.
« Pour moi, la démocratie, c’est un système politique qui appelle à la participation de toutes les personnes composant une entité ou logées dans un territoire donné. Ce sont ces personnes qui devraient confier leur pouvoir de décision, notamment celui relatif au fonctionnement et surtout au bon fonctionnement de leur société, à un seul individu ou à quelques individus chargés de les représenter », a-t-il expliqué.
Lire aussi :  « Il y a absolument beaucoup d’opposants, c’est ça la valeur de notre démocratie », sénateur Abderaman Koulamallah
Cette conférence publique se veut ainsi un espace de réflexion et de dialogue sur la place des jeunes dans la vie démocratique tchadienne, mais aussi sur leur responsabilité dans la prévention des conflits et la promotion d’une paix durable.

items.title: Sénégal : le maire d'Oulampane grièvement brûlé par sa première épouse

original_payload.original_title: Sénégal : le maire d'Oulampane grièvement brûlé par sa première épouse
original_payload.original_body:
Afrique
Sénégal : le maire d'Oulampane grièvement brûlé par sa première épouse
Le maire d'Oulampane, au sud du Sénégal, a été grièvement brûlé à son domicile. Sa première épouse a été interpellée et placée en garde à vue.
Alwihda Info
28 nov. 2026
Par Temandang Gontran
Le maire de la commune d'Oulampane, dans le département de Bignona au sud du Sénégal, Sagar Coly, a été grièvement brûlé le jeudi 26 novembre 2026 à son domicile, dans une affaire qui suscite une vive émotion dans le pays.
Selon les informations rapportées par plusieurs médias sénégalais, l'édile aurait été aspergé d'un liquide inflammable pendant son sommeil, avant que le feu ne soit déclenché dans sa chambre. Grièvement atteint, il a été secouru par des proches et des voisins, puis évacué vers l'hôpital de Bignona avant d'être transféré au centre hospitalier régional de Ziguinchor. Son état demeure préoccupant, bien que des sources hospitalières indiquent qu'il est actuellement stable.
Les premiers éléments de l'enquête désignent sa première épouse comme principale suspecte. D'après les autorités, celle-ci aurait pris la fuite en direction de la Gambie avant d'être interpellée par les gendarmes à Bounkiling. Placée en garde à vue, elle aurait reconnu les faits lors de son audition, invoquant un profond conflit conjugal lié au récent remariage de son époux dans le cadre d'une union polygame.
Une enquête a été ouverte afin d'établir les circonstances exactes de ce drame et de déterminer les responsabilités. Les autorités judiciaires poursuivent leurs investigations, tandis que cette affaire relance le débat sur les violences au sein du couple.
Cette agression a provoqué une forte onde de choc au Sénégal, où l'opinion publique attend désormais les conclusions de l'enquête et les suites judiciaires qui seront réservées à ce dossier.

items.title: Tchad : à Fada, inauguration d'une mosquée offerte par le chef de l'État

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : à Fada, inauguration d'une mosquée offerte par le chef de l'État
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
Tchad : à Fada, inauguration d'une mosquée offerte par le chef de l'État
Inaugurée à Fada dans l'Ennedi-Ouest, une nouvelle mosquée de 500 m² a été offerte par le président Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno pour honorer la mémoire de son ami d'enfance, Hassan Guihini Hemissa.
Alwihda Info
28 nov. 2026
© DR
Le délégué général du gouvernement auprès de la province de l'Ennedi-Ouest, le contrôleur général de police Goukouni Allatchi Tchougoubou, a inauguré vendredi la nouvelle mosquée Hassan Guihini Hemissa à Fada. La cérémonie s'est déroulée en présence de plusieurs personnalités, parmi lesquelles le président du CNAIT, Cheikh Abdeldaïm Abdoulaye Ousmane, et le ministre des Télécommunications, Haliki Choua Mahamat.
Offerte par le président de la République, le maréchal Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno, cette infrastructure religieuse a été construite pour honorer la mémoire de son ami d'enfance, Hassan Guihini Hemissa, affectueusement appelé Kouakou.
Bâtie sur une superficie de 500 m², la mosquée comprend un espace de prière, un logement pour l'imam, un local technique ainsi qu'un mini-château d'eau. Réalisée par l'entreprise Hor, cette réalisation vise à offrir aux fidèles des conditions optimales pour l'accomplissement de leurs pratiques religieuses et à renforcer l'apprentissage du Saint Coran.

items.title: CEEAC : le retrait du Rwanda officiellement acté

original_payload.original_title: CEEAC : le retrait du Rwanda officiellement acté
original_payload.original_body:
La Communauté économique des États de l'Afrique centrale (CEEAC) a officiellement pris acte du retrait du Rwanda vendredi 27 novembre 2026 à l'issue d'une Conférence des chefs d'État et de gouvernement, tenue à Sipopo, en Guinée équatoriale. Le Rwanda avait annoncé son retrait de l'organisation en juin 2025. Kigali dénonçait alors une "dérive" de cette organisation favorable à la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) sur fond de conflit dans l'est de ce pays.
La Conférence des chefs d'Etats de la CEEAC avait prolongé d'une année supplémentaire le mandat du président équatoguinéen Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogoa à la tête de l'organisation, alors que Kigali devait en prendre la tête.
Dans son communiqué du vendredi, la Conférence indique avoir examiné l'évolution du dossier et les discussions autour du départ de Kigali.  "Prenant acte du retrait de la République du Rwanda",  les dirigeants ont notamment demandé que les dispositions administratives, juridiques et financières soient mises en œuvre pour officialiser le départ du pays de l'organisation. Ce départ s'inscrit dans un contexte de tensions entre Kigali et Kinshasa, marqué par le conflit dans l'est de la RDC et les accusations de soutien rwandais aux rebelles du M23.
Cinq chefs d'État ont pris part aux travaux de la conférence : Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo pour la Guinée équatoriale, Félix Tshisekedi pour la RDC, Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema pour le Gabon, Carlos Vila Nova pour Sao Tomé-et-Principe et Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno pour le Tchad.
La présidence tournante de l'organisation aux 10 pays membres en l'absence du Rwanda : Angola, Burundi, Cameroun, Gabon, Guinée équatoriale, République centrafricaine, République démocratique du Congo (RDC), République du Congo, São Tomé-et-Príncipe et Tchad, a été confiée au président tchadien, Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno.
Une passation symbolique du drapeau communautaire a marqué le transfert entre le président sortant, Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, et son successeur. Le prochain sommet de l'organisation est prévu en février 2027 à N'Djamena.

items.title: N’Djamena : « Enfant lecteur », une bibliothèque gratuite pour réconcilier les enfants avec les livres

original_payload.original_title: N’Djamena : « Enfant lecteur », une bibliothèque gratuite pour réconcilier les enfants avec les livres
original_payload.original_body:
À N’Djamena, une nouvelle initiative entend rapprocher les enfants des livres et faire de la lecture un véritable plaisir. Baptisée « Enfant lecteur », cette bibliothèque gratuite, spécialement destinée aux enfants de la maternelle jusqu’au collège, ambitionne de développer la culture de la lecture dès le plus jeune âge.
Après l’expérience de la bibliothèque ambulante installée dans un véhicule, la capitale tchadienne accueille ainsi un nouvel espace consacré à la promotion du livre et de la lecture. À l’occasion du mois dédié aux livres et à la lecture, le ministre du Développement touristique, de la Culture et de l’Artisanat, Abakar Rozzi Téguil, a effectué, ce samedi 28 novembre 2026, une visite au sein de cette bibliothèque.
Sur place, le membre du gouvernement a découvert des rayons garnis de romans, de bandes dessinées et d’encyclopédies, accessibles aux jeunes lecteurs. Une initiative qu’il a saluée et encouragée, estimant qu’elle offre aux enfants une occasion de se familiariser très tôt avec la lecture.  « Nous venons vraiment d’être surpris par ces bibliothèques, avec ces rayons pleins de romans, de bandes dessinées et surtout d’encyclopédies » , a-t-il déclaré.
Le ministre a également invité d’autres acteurs à s’inspirer de cette expérience afin de multiplier les espaces de lecture au profit des enfants et des jeunes. Il a particulièrement salué l’engagement de Dr Gani Daoussa, initiatrice du projet, tout en l’encourageant à poursuivre et à élargir cette démarche. Il a, par ailleurs, lancé un appel aux enfants à fréquenter régulièrement cet espace, rappelant que «  lire, c’est apprendre, lire, c’est voyager, lire, c’est rêver  ».
Pour Dr Gani Daoussa, la visite du ministre constitue un signe d’encouragement et témoigne de l’importance accordée à la promotion des bibliothèques. Elle déplore notamment le manque de bibliothèques scolaires dans plusieurs établissements, alors que la lecture joue un rôle essentiel dans le développement intellectuel et l’épanouissement des enfants.
Au-delà de la mise à disposition des livres, la philosophie de la bibliothèque « Enfant lecteur » repose sur une approche qui consiste à réconcilier les enfants avec la lecture en la sortant du cadre contraignant des devoirs scolaires.  « La philosophie derrière cette bibliothèque, c’est de ne pas considérer la lecture comme un moyen de punition ou de devoir, mais plutôt de goûter à la lecture, de voir la lecture comme un plaisir » , explique-t-elle.
Dans un environnement où les écrans et les tablettes occupent une place grandissante dans le quotidien des enfants, Dr Gani Daoussa estime que le livre conserve une valeur irremplaçable. Pour elle, la lecture permet aux jeunes de découvrir de nouveaux horizons, de stimuler leur imagination et d'acquérir des connaissances qu'aucun autre support ne peut entièrement remplacer.
Avec cette bibliothèque gratuite, l'ambition est donc de faire du livre un compagnon quotidien des enfants et de contribuer, dès le plus jeune âge, à la construction d'une génération davantage attachée au savoir et à la lecture.

items.title: Batha : Six groupements féminins reçoivent des kits pour développer leurs activités économiques

original_payload.original_title: Batha : Six groupements féminins reçoivent des kits pour développer leurs activités économiques
original_payload.original_body:
Batha : Six groupements féminins reçoivent des kits pour développer leurs activités économiques
admin
novembre 28, 2026
2 minutes lues
58 vues
Six groupements féminins de la province du Batha ont bénéficié de kits de matériel à l’issue d’une formation sur la transformation des produits locaux. Organisée par Impact Ladies International, en partenariat avec la North American Chadian Initiative (NACI), la session a pris fin ce samedi 28 novembre 2026 au centre ALNAHADA d’Ati.
Durant quatre jours, des femmes venues de différentes localités du Batha et d’autres provinces du pays ont été formées à plusieurs techniques de transformation des produits locaux. Elles ont notamment appris à fabriquer du savon, à préparer de la viande séchée, à transformer les produits laitiers et à valoriser l’huile de neem.
Les participantes ont été encadrées par des formatrices venues de N’Djamena, de Koundoul et d’Ati. La formation leur a également permis de partager leurs expériences et de renforcer leurs connaissances dans différents domaines de production.
À la clôture, six groupements féminins ont reçu des kits de matériel pour mettre en pratique les compétences acquises et développer leurs activités génératrices de revenus.
À travers cette initiative, Impact Ladies International et son partenaire NACI souhaitent encourager l’entrepreneuriat féminin et aider les femmes à mieux exploiter les ressources locales. L’ambition est de leur permettre de développer des activités durables et de renforcer progressivement leur autonomie financière.
TWM/ Soumaine Rahama

items.title: Court rejects Argentina’s request to stop UK oil activity near Falklands

original_payload.original_title: Court rejects Argentina’s request to stop UK oil activity near Falklands
original_payload.original_body:
An international court has rejected Argentina’s request for provisional measures to halt United Kingdom-authorised oil drilling near the Falkland Islands.
Saturday’s ruling by the United Nations-backed International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea is a setback to Buenos Aires’s latest effort to challenge economic activity around the disputed territory.
Recommended Stories

list 2 of 4  What’s at stake in the renewed tensions over the Falkland Islands?
list 3 of 4  Argentina’s Milei threatens legal action over Falklands oil project

Argentina’s request marks the latest spat between the two countries, which fought a brief but bitter 74-day war in 1982 over the UK-administered islands in the South Atlantic.
In September, Argentina launched an arbitration process against London over the Sea Lion project off the Falklands, which is led by the UK’s Rockhopper company and Israel’s Navitas.
Buenos Aires has argued the plan violates a UN resolution calling for both sides to desist from unilateral actions until their dispute over the sovereignty of the islands is resolved.
It has asked the court to impose emergency measures and order the UK to take the necessary steps “to ensure that no new drilling for exploitation, and no installation of production infrastructure” takes place in the North Malvinas Basin.
It further urged the Hamburg-based court, an independent court set up under UN auspices, to order the UK to “refrain from using the information obtained in the exploration of the natural resources of the disputed maritime areas”.
original_payload.original_summary: An international tribunal refuses Buenos Aires's application, giving the green light to the project off the disputed region.

items.title: Bootleg alcohol poisonings in Iran see dozens dead and badly injured

original_payload.original_title: Bootleg alcohol poisonings in Iran see dozens dead and badly injured
original_payload.original_body:
Two years after four people were executed for distributing contaminated alcoholic beverages – causing the deaths of 17 people and leaving 199 with injuries, including blindness – another spate of mass alcohol poisoning has swept through Iran.
Since mid-November, more than 20 people have died and at least 500 have been poisoned from consuming methanol-contaminated alcohol, the same substance used in medical disinfectants and wound care, and potentially fatal if consumed.

items.title: Norse Atlantic ends flights: How Iran war continues to batter aviation

original_payload.original_title: Norse Atlantic ends flights: How Iran war continues to batter aviation

The Norwegian airline Norse Atlantic has filed for bankruptcy for its main operating unit, cancelling all flights and halting ticket sales, as soaring jet fuel prices triggered by the United States-Israel  war on Iran  claim another operator.
The long-haul, low-cost carrier said on Friday that it  had failed to secure the short-term financing  it needs to keep flying.

It joins a growing list of carriers that have collapsed, entered restructuring or cut routes since the US-Israel war on Iran began in late February and disrupted shipping through the  Strait of Hormuz , a key artery for Gulf oil and refined fuel exports.
Here is what we know.
Why has Norse Atlantic stopped flying?
The board of the airline’s Norwegian operating subsidiary, Norse Atlantic Airways AS, filed a bankruptcy petition with the Agder District Court on Friday, after concluding there was “no longer a basis for continued operations”.
The filing came a day after the airline suspended all flights, and two days after it warned that its financial position was “critical”. Its shares closed 85 percent lower on Thursday.
“If a short-term financing solution is not secured urgently, it is the board’s intention to file for bankruptcy,” the company said as it grounded its fleet.
A day later, it confirmed that no rescue had materialised. “Despite extensive efforts, the company has so far not been able to secure sufficient funding to meet its short-term liquidity needs,” Norse Atlantic ASA said.
“We were unable to absorb the extra cost … Fuel is what toppled this company,” Chief Executive Officer Eivind Roald told Norwegian public broadcaster NRK.

India ⁠were 116-6 at stumps in reply to the Black Caps’ first innings 356, with Dhruv Jurel on seven not out and tailender Akash Deep next in the line of fire after Washington Sundar’s dismissal for 10 wrapped up play.

It was ⁠a formidable display by the home quicks, who shared the wickets around and had the ball swinging wildly on a tricky Hagley Oval pitch.

Smith landed a hammer blow with the final ball of the day, having Sundar edge a short ball to captain Tom Latham in the slips, ending ‌a tortured, 60-ball knock.

original_payload.original_title: Israel unity government talks stall: What happens now?
original_payload.original_body:
The future of Israel’s government remains unclear following October elections that produced no clear winner.
The leader of the centrist Yashar party, Gadi Eisenkot, and his main rival, caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party, have been convening for rounds of talks in a bid to establish a “unity government”.

But the talks ended on Sunday without a conclusive deal, with the two parties announcing that a “follow-up” meeting will be held soon.
So, what is the latest on the talks? And what happens if they fail to reach an agreement?
Here’s what we know.
Why are Eisenkot and Netanyahu in talks?
Following the October 27 general election, Israeli President Isaac Herzog  held consultations  with political parties to decide who he would appoint to form a government after neither side secured a majority. Eisenkot and his presumed partners won 48 seats between them, while Netanyahu’s alliance won 53.
Some 67 lawmakers, including from Arab-led parties, endorsed Eisenkot to form the next government, while only 46 backed Netanyahu.
In November, Eisenkot was  instructed  by Israel’s president to form a new government by December 6, with a deadline that can be extended by 14 days.
In order to form a government, one party, alliance or coalition requires a minimum 61 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. This means Eisenkot must ally with other parties or lawmakers to make up the seat numbers.
Arab-led parties, representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, won a record 19 seats in the election. But Eisenkot has ruled out forming a government with them, which would have given him a 67-seat bloc. Winning over Israel’s two ultra-Orthodox parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas, would give him exactly 61 seats.

items.title: The perfect storm behind Congo’s deadliest Ebola outbreak

original_payload.original_title: The perfect storm behind Congo’s deadliest Ebola outbreak
original_payload.original_body:
When crises collide
“The people here live in poverty and insecurity; every day is a struggle to survive,” said Congolese physician Alex Bonane Murutsi, who works at the Ebola treatment centre in Bunia where Vandamme did her field assignment. Murutsi started working in the MSF Ebola response after contracting the deadly Bundibugyo virus and fighting for his life for 18 days earlier this year.
“The epidemic makes their already difficult life even harder. For many, it’s hard to accept the prevention measures,” he said.
He has seen families resist safe burials and Ebola survivors face exclusion and stigma. Funerals traditionally involve a lot of touching, dancing around and washing the body of the deceased — rituals that are important to the local culture. Safe burials require isolating the body in a sealed bag to prevent viral transmission. Distrust in Ebola response workers and the inability to perform the traditional rites and say a proper farewell cause some families to hide deaths or resist safe burials.
As for survivors’ stigma, local populations do not always understand that recovered patients are no longer infectious, leading to fear and avoidance due to a lack of public information or misinformation. Even health workers can get a hard time from their own families, Murutsi explained, because they don’t always understand how they can safely work in a treatment centre.
Dr Alex Bonane Murutsi started working in the MSF Ebola response after contracting the deadly Bundibugyo virus and fighting for his life for 18 days at an MSF Ebola treatment centre [Julien Dewarichet/ MSF]   “In the beginning, there was not enough communication. People didn’t always understand why certain measures were necessary,” he explained.
That mistrust sometimes turns violent. One of the soft-spoken doctor’s colleagues was working at a rural health post when a patient suffering from severe bleeding was brought in. The medical staff voiced their suspicion of Ebola, which infuriated the patient’s companions. They insisted the disease did not exist in their village and accused the health workers of bringing it there. The doctor was assaulted and had to flee.
But Dr Murutsi stresses that medical teams do not face hostility everywhere. In Bunia, there is more trust, partly because local health workers engage directly with the community.
“People know us and we take the time to explain why certain measures are important. You don’t earn people’s trust by simply telling them what to do; you have to talk to them,” he explained.
Anna Halford is acutely aware of the challenges of fighting Ebola in conditions of insecurity. The British aid worker coordinates MSF’s response to the outbreak across the DRC.
“The physical access to some of the affected areas is severely compromised,” she said. “This makes it extremely difficult to transport supplies and establish proper screening and surveillance.”
In some conflict-affected areas, violence and insecurity prevent health teams from reaching communities, leaving sick people with little or no access to Ebola testing and care. This also hampers contact tracing, which is crucial for fighting the virus. For every confirmed case, teams must quickly identify people who may have been exposed and monitor them for three weeks after their last known contact.
Halford, an experienced humanitarian who also helped tackle the largest-ever West African Ebola outbreak, emphasised that violence is not the only obstacle to taming the virus.
“Several areas not affected by armed groups are also seeing a rise in cases and struggling with the response,” she pointed out.
Supply routes are not only cut off by the risk of attacks, but also by the country’s weak infrastructure. Patients often have to travel for hours along bumpy roads to reach a treatment centre. Meanwhile, medicines and medical supplies often fail to reach remote villages in good condition.
This leaves front line health workers across the whole DRC without the basic protective equipment needed to safely treat suspected Ebola patients. Halford recently encountered this in a remote clinic far from the conflict-ridden East.
“In an area where, thankfully, numbers are still low, medical workers were forced to make do with makeshift protective gear designed for COVID-19 and flip-flops,” she said, expressing her frustration.
Responding to Ebola is an inherently complex and costly operation. According to the veteran field worker, the security risks act as a disease multiplier, further exacerbated by the crippling lack of funding that Congolese health services historically struggled with.
This longstanding problem has only grown worse in recent years, since international donations have sharply declined. Last year, the United Nations’ humanitarian emergency response plan for the Congo was funded by  barely a quarter  of the required amount.
Jeremy Konyndyk, who led the US response to the Ebola outbreak in West Africa in 2014 and now heads Refugees International,  argued on the Zeteo  media website that the dismantling of USAID played a role in the delayed detection. The US Agency for International Development (USAID) previously deployed rapid response teams, known as DART, to detect and contain outbreaks.
With them gone, the early warning system failed, allowing the virus to circulate undetected from February through May. According to him, the cuts also contributed to shortages of protective equipment and limited the capacity to analyse samples and conduct tests.
The collapse of USAID hit even harder because other donors — such as the United Kingdom, Germany, France, and Canada — cut back on aid almost simultaneously,  according  to epidemiologist Alain Casseus, head of the infectious diseases division of the leading medical charity Partners in Health.
As a result, the Congolese Ministry of Health and Africa CDC were initially left largely on their own to tackle the raging epidemic with limited staff and supplies.
The fragile Congolese healthcare system was quickly overwhelmed.
Early Ebola symptoms resemble those of malaria or typhoid, and infections were often misidentified in understaffed and poorly equipped health centres. After the outbreak was officially declared in May, it took months to bring the testing capacity up to the required level.
Halford is relieved that the international community has recently stepped up efforts to close the funding gap. In September, new pledges from G20 foreign ministers and major donors brought total global commitments since May to around $2.9bn.
“I’m delighted that there have been some donors, and the Congolese state itself, which have pledged and disbursed resources,” she said. “But for whatever reason, we are not seeing enough of the effect of those resources on the ground.”
That mismatch is apparently so striking that Javid Abdelmoneim, the international president of MSF, sounded the alarm earlier this month. In a scathing  statement , he warned that the funds simply have not reached the front lines of the fight against Ebola.
“Despite the vast amounts of money provided for the response, many front-line responders are left trying to contain the outbreak with empty hands and empty pockets,” Abdelmomein said in an MSF statement.
“Our teams are often left speechless by the dysfunctions they witness. Six months into the response, this situation is simply unacceptable.”
Abdelmomein cites cases of untrained and unpaid health workers, ambulances unable to respond due to lack of fuel and phantom surveillance teams that exist on spreadsheets but are nowhere to be seen in the field.
Despite funding earmarked for this crucial work, a comprehensive system to detect infections and trace contacts is still lacking, Abdelmomein said.
“In Ituri, only nine percent of patients with Ebola disease treated by our teams had previously been identified as contacts by the surveillance system,” Abdelmomein added.
Halford, his coworker, claims there’s a serious lack of oversight of how pledged funds reach operations on the ground. But according to her, there’s no single explanation or culprit to point fingers at.
“This is not a criticism directed at the DRC government, which itself denounced that lack of transparency. Poor planning and oversight lead to many overlapping aid projects in one area, while others are left neglected,” she said.
Halford notes that the specific circumstances in DRC, where one of the deadliest viruses in the world strikes in a war-torn region with a historically weak health system, make an already difficult Ebola response extremely hard.
“Tackling Ebola requires everything, everywhere, all at once. It’s an uphill battle, but it is a collective responsibility to overcome these challenges in order to stop this devastating virus,” she added.
original_payload.original_summary: Patients and health workers pay a staggering cost as war and a failing health system collide with a deadly virus.

items.title: Two visions of Spain collide as voters weigh PM Sanchez’s record

original_payload.original_title: Two visions of Spain collide as voters weigh PM Sanchez’s record
original_payload.original_body:
Madrid, Spain   –  Voters in Spain are set to  head to the polls  in an election that could open the door to the far right entering the country’s national government, half a century after the end of Francisco Franco’s dictatorship.
After a bitter campaign largely focused on housing and immigration, Sunday’s snap vote pits two sharply different accounts of socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s eight years in power against each other. One says the country has become a bastion of social progress and a driver of economic growth in a largely stagnant Europe. The other, embraced by the opposition conservatives and the far right, says Spain needs a profound change after years of alleged corruption and opportunism.
Recommended Stories
